title: Quantum Phase Transitions And Quantum-information Characterization Of A non-Hermitian Xy Chain With Staggered Dzyaloshinskii--Moriya Interactions

abstract: ArXiv:2609.05470v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate the phase diagram of a non-Hermitian XY chain with staggered Dzyaloshinskii--Moriya (DM) interactions using quantum-information methods. Moreover, measurements of QC along different directions capture the DM-induced relative rotation between the two sublattices, thereby distinguishing the staggered-DM chain from a zero-DM chain with identical effective parameters.

title: Quantum Information Spreading Via Higher-order Operator Correlators
abstract: ArXiv:2609.05472v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We provide a perspective into measuring the quantum information spreading by introducing N-operator correlators. abstract: ArXiv:2609.05625v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: One of the strengths of our recently proposed Walking Cat Architecture for a trapped-ion quantum computer is that it is straightforward to extend and optimize for a specific application. We optimize the circuits from Schrottenloher's recent work and arrive at a logical quantum circuit for solving the ECDLP using about [MATH] qubits and [MATH] Toffoli gates, with a rigorous lower bound on the logical-level success probability that holds with confidence at least [MATH]. Using our compilation toolchain with manual optimization of the logical layout and integrated routing, we produce estimates for the logical measurement depth and the required number of physical qubits by compiling all components to measurement schedules that obey the architectural constraints. title: Hawking Radiation In non-Hermitian Microscopic Analogues

abstract: ArXiv:2609.05632v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Non-Hermitian systems have recently emerged as a convenient platform to realize black-hole physics. title: Phase-cycled Randomized Benchmarking Of Quantum Processors: Recovering Hidden Classical Noise Correlations

abstract: ArXiv:2609.06448v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Randomized benchmarking can hide classical temporal correlations because its Clifford-twirled response is even in the noise phase. title: Information Loss Under Gauge Reduction Of Discrete Electromagnetic Fields
abstract: ArXiv:2609.05473v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study relative entropy under gauge reduction in Whitney-discretized electromagnetism. The discrete Hodge decomposition separates exact gauge directions from harmonic and coexact physical degrees of freedom. For Gaussian distributions on the auxiliary potential space, relative entropy splits exactly into the relative entropy of the physical marginals and a nonnegative conditional gauge contribution. We express this contribution through Schur complements, conditional means, and physical--gauge correlations, and characterize equality between auxiliary and physical relative entropies. The physical divergence is also shown to be the minimum over all Gaussian auxiliary extensions. At the infinitesimal level, Fisher information admits an analogous decomposition. A two-variable model illustrates how statistically distinct auxiliary potentials may represent identical physical statistics. The construction provides an information-geometric interpretation of discrete gauge reduction without assigning physical significance to the eliminated gauge variables.
tldr: The paper studies how relative entropy and Fisher information decompose under gauge reduction in discrete electromagnetic field theory, showing that auxiliary potential distributions contain a nonnegative gauge contribution that vanishes when physical marginals are identical.
motivation: To understand the information-theoretic consequences of eliminating gauge degrees of freedom in discrete electromagnetism, and to clarify that gauge variables carry no physical significance yet affect statistical distances.
method: The author applies Whitney discretization and Hodge decomposition to separate exact (gauge) from physical (harmonic and coexact) parts, then considers Gaussian distributions on the auxiliary potential space and computes relative entropy via Schur complements and conditional means.
result: Relative entropy between auxiliary distributions splits exactly into the relative entropy of the physical marginals plus a nonnegative conditional gauge term; the physical divergence is the minimum over all Gaussian extensions, and Fisher information decomposes analogously.
conclusion: The work provides an information-geometric interpretation of gauge reduction, showing that statistically distinct gauge potentials can yield identical physical statistics without implying physical information loss.

title: Matrix Product Belief Propagation
authors: Gabriel Woolls, Shahin Jahanbani, Adarsh Pashikanti, Matthew T. Fishman, Joseph Tindall, Michael P. Zaletel
abstract: ArXiv:2609.05598v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce "matrix product belief propagation" (MP-BP) as a controlled method for the approximate contraction of two-dimensional tensor networks and graphical models, which generically leads to a quadratic reduction of errors relative to existing methods: at similar computational effort, the number of accurate digits is asymptotically doubled. For infinite systems, MP-BP can be understood as a practical implementation of Baxter's corner-transfer-matrix method; for reflection-symmetric networks, it further coincides with the boundary matrix-product-state and corner-transfer-matrix renormalization group algorithms as conventionally implemented. In the limit of unit matrix-product rank, MP-BP is equivalent to belief propagation, and more generally, can be understood as a generalization of BP in which the "messages" live on surfaces and are assumed to have a matrix-product factorization. We further extend the quadratic improvement to the computation of expectation values, and numerically demonstrate the qualitatively improved convergence for a variety of classical and quantum 2D tensor network problems.
tldr: Introduces MP-BP, a controlled approximate contraction method for 2D tensor networks that achieves quadratic error reduction over existing methods.
motivation: Contracting 2D tensor networks accurately is computationally challenging; existing methods like belief propagation have limited precision.
method: Generalizes belief propagation by assuming messages live on surfaces with a matrix-product factorization, enabling a practical implementation of corner transfer matrix methods.
result: Demonstrates asymptotically doubled accuracy in the number of correct digits at similar computational effort, with improved convergence for classical and quantum problems.
conclusion: MP-BP is a robust and efficient algorithm for tensor network contraction, with broad applicability but not directly aligned with the specified research directions.

title: Distribution Of Currents In A System Of Active Particles With Biased Hops And Ising Interactions
authors: Evgeniy Khain, Shriram Ramesh, Vladimir Chernyak
abstract: ArXiv:2609.05649v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider an ensemble of particles performing a biased random walk on a two-dimensional lattice. Due to the adhesion between particles (nearest-neighbor Ising interactions), the probability of hopping depends on the number of neighbors and the strength of adhesive interaction. The asymmetry in the hopping directions leads to a macroscopic current of particles through the system. We theoretically compute the distribution of currents and verify the results in stochastic particle simulations. To make theoretical progress, one has to determine the probabilities of various particle configurations such as single particles, pairs, and different configurations of three-particle clusters. These probabilities are theoretically derived by formulating rate equations for the concentrations of various structures resembling Becker-D\"oring cluster equations. One intriguing finding is that the concentration of left-handed triplets is not equal to the concentration of right-handed triplets for non-zero asymmetry of hops and non-zero interaction between particles.
tldr: This paper analyzes current distributions in a classical lattice gas of active particles with biased hops and Ising interactions, deriving cluster rate equations and verifying via simulations.
motivation: To understand non-equilibrium current fluctuations in interacting particle systems and explain an observed asymmetry in chiral triplet concentrations.
method: The authors formulate rate equations for concentrations of particle clusters (singles, pairs, triples) analogous to Becker-Döring equations, and validate theoretical predictions with stochastic particle simulations.
result: The paper derives the current distribution and finds that left-handed and right-handed triplets occur with unequal concentrations under asymmetric hopping and interactions.
conclusion: The study provides a theoretical framework for current statistics in active matter systems, highlighting chiral symmetry breaking in cluster populations, but it does not align with the specified research directions on quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid systems.

title: Characterizing Privacy Risks Of Quantum Machine Learning With Emergent Quantum-Native Access
authors: Liou Tang, James Joshi, Ashish Kundu
abstract: ArXiv:2609.05702v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Quantum Machine Learning (QML) has shown rapid advances by utilizing quantum computing for machine learning tasks. Meanwhile, the privacy risks accompanying QML is also starting to be studied, which inherit privacy leakage channels from "classical" ML and also quantum-unique risks. Existing work on privacy-preserving QML largely focuses on a QML-as-a-service scenario, which generally assumes that the QML model owner provides only classical bit outputs to queries, while users (and adversaries) have only classical computing abilities. However, this view is increasingly challenged in a quantum-native world of quantum-capable users/adversaries, which may have access to both quantum computing abilities and access to quantum information output from service providers. In this paper, we aim to bridge this gap by examining membership inference attacks against QML models by demonstrating that increasing quantum access and quantum computing abilities provides provable theoretical privacy leakage and empirical adversarial gain. However, the probabilistic nature of QML introduces a gap between theoretical and empirical adversarial advantage. These results show that existing research on privacy leakage on QML models underestimate privacy leakage in an emergent quantum-native access regimes, which we hope to establish a first step into examining potential privacy leakages for QML in the quantum-native world.These results show that existing research on privacy leakage in QML models underestimates privacy leakage in emergent quantum-native access regimes, and we hope to establish a first step in examining potential privacy leakages for QML in the quantum-native world.
tldr: This paper investigates membership inference attacks on quantum machine learning models in a quantum-native setting, showing that increased quantum access and computing power lead to greater privacy leakage.
motivation: Existing privacy research on QML assumes classical-only adversaries and outputs, underestimating risks in future quantum-native environments where users may have quantum capabilities and receive quantum information.
method: The authors analyze membership inference attacks against QML models under varying levels of quantum access and computing abilities, providing theoretical proofs of privacy leakage and conducting empirical adversarial experiments.
result: They demonstrate that quantum-native access and quantum computing abilities increase both theoretical and empirical privacy leakage, but observe a gap between the two due to the probabilistic nature of QML.
conclusion: The findings indicate that current privacy analyses of QML underestimate risks in quantum-native settings, highlighting the need for further research on privacy attacks and defenses in the quantum-native world.

title: Saqc: A SAT-Aware Compilation Framework For QAOA-Based Quantum Optimization
authors: Till Schnittka, Julie Maria Raju, Abhoy Kole, Rolf Drechsler
abstract: ArXiv:2609.05737v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm (QAOA) is a promising variational approach for solving Boolean satisfiability (SAT) problems. Existing SAT-to-QAOA workflows first translate Boolean formulas into penalty Hamiltonians before applying generic quantum compilation, thereby discarding SAT-specific information such as clause structure, logical operators, and variable dependencies. Consequently, subsequent compiler optimizations cannot exploit the underlying Boolean formulation. This paper presents SAQC, a SAT-aware compilation framework that introduces a SAT Intermediate Representation (SIR) to preserve Boolean structure during compilation. The proposed framework supports both CNF and XOR-extended CNF (eCNF) formulations and performs SAT-aware optimizations including clause rewriting, dependency analysis, and clause scheduling prior to quantum lowering. Building on the optimized SIR, SAQC provides a unified framework for both penalty Hamiltonian generation and direct clause-to-ansatz synthesis, together with ansatz optimizations based on relative-phase decomposition, ancilla-assisted synthesis, and dynamic uncomputation. Experimental results demonstrate significant reductions in circuit depth, two-qubit gate count, and compilation time compared with conventional Hamiltonian-based workflows while remaining compatible with existing quantum compilation frameworks.
tldr: SAQC is a SAT-aware compilation framework that preserves Boolean structure to optimize QAOA circuits for solving SAT problems.
motivation: Existing SAT-to-QAOA workflows discard useful Boolean information during translation, limiting compiler optimizations.
method: The framework introduces a SAT Intermediate Representation (SIR) and performs SAT-aware optimizations (clause rewriting, dependency analysis, scheduling) before quantum lowering, supporting both CNF and XOR-extended CNF, and offers unified generation of penalty Hamiltonians or direct clause-to-ansatz synthesis with additional optimizations.
result: Experiments show significant reductions in circuit depth, two-qubit gate count, and compilation time compared to conventional Hamiltonian-based workflows.
conclusion: SAQC improves quantum compilation efficiency for QAOA-based SAT solvers while maintaining compatibility with existing frameworks.

title: Foundations Of Many-Body Theory Of Quantum Unified Statistics: Green Functions And Linear Response Theory
authors: M. Beyrami, M. N. Najafi, H. Esmaili, M. Dournama, H. Mohammadzadeh
abstract: ArXiv:2609.05878v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop a comprehensive many-body theory for systems of particles obeying quantum unified statistics, or quons. After exploring the properties of the Fock space of this system, we formulate a systematic S-matrix expansion and a generalized Wick's theorem. A consistent Green-function formalism is constructed at both zero and finite temperatures, accompanied by a generalized Wick's theorem appropriate for infinite-statistics operator algebras. Within this framework, we establish diagrammatic rules for interacting quon systems. Employing the random phase approximation, we derive the dielectric function and reveal the emergence of anomalous plasmon modes that have no direct counterpart in conventional Bose or Fermi systems. We further analyze the ground-state energy, energy-loss function, generalized Thomas-Fermi screening wave vectors, and Friedel oscillations, elucidating how infinite statistics qualitatively modifies collective behavior and screening properties.
tldr: Develops a comprehensive many-body theory for particles obeying quantum unified statistics (quons), deriving Green functions and linear response to reveal anomalous plasmons and modified screening.
motivation: To understand collective and screening properties of systems with infinite statistics, which have no direct counterpart in conventional Bose or Fermi systems.
method: Constructs Fock space, formulates S-matrix expansion and generalized Wick's theorem, develops Green-function formalism at zero and finite temperatures, and applies random phase approximation.
result: Derives dielectric function showing anomalous plasmon modes, analyzes ground-state energy, energy-loss function, Thomas-Fermi screening wave vectors, and Friedel oscillations altered by infinite statistics.
conclusion: Infinite statistics qualitatively modify collective excitations and screening, providing a foundation for studying quon systems.

title: Rapid And High-sensitive NV-based Microwave Field Imaging Via Digital Lock-in Amplification For On-chip Microstrip Diagnostics
authors: Zijin Fu, Yanjie Liu, Hongliang Wu, Yuchen Han, Zhengtao Wang, Haolin Li, Dezhi Zheng, Bo Zhang, Jun Zhang
abstract: ArXiv:2609.05886v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: High-resolution, high-sensitivity microwave (MW) magnetic field imaging is indispensable for non-destructive integrated circuit (IC) testing, radio-frequency device characterization, and spintronic research. Yet, the practical utility of these techniques is severely constrained by the pervasive challenge of isolating weak magnetic signatures from intense optical and electronic noise, which fundamentally limits both acquisition speed and detection sensitivity. Here, we overcome this barrier by introducing a wide-field imaging scheme based on an ensemble of diamond nitrogen-vacancy (NV) centers, synergistically combined with digital lock-in amplification (DLA). By exploiting digital demodulation, the DLA precisely extracts the MW-field response at a specific modulation frequency from background noise (e.g., laser intensity fluctuations), dramatically improving the signal-to-noise ratio (SNR). Consequently, our system attains a magnetic field sensitivity of 126 nT/[MATH]. Critically, the unprecedented SNR permits a pixel dwell time of under one millisecond, allowing full-field images to be acquired within seconds-more than an order of magnitude faster than state-of-the-art NV-based wide-field techniques. This combination of speed, sensitivity, and micron-scale spatial resolution (1.6 [MATH]m) paves the way for quasi-real-time, non-invasive diagnostics of dynamic MW devices and integrated circuits.
tldr: This paper presents a wide-field microwave magnetic field imaging technique using NV centers in diamond with digital lock-in amplification, achieving high sensitivity and speed for on-chip diagnostics.
motivation: To address the challenge of isolating weak magnetic signals from background noise in NV-based microwave imaging, which limits acquisition speed and detection sensitivity.
method: The method combines an ensemble of nitrogen-vacancy (NV) centers with digital lock-in amplification (DLA) to extract the MW-field response at a specific modulation frequency, enhancing the signal-to-noise ratio.
result: The system achieves a magnetic field sensitivity of 126 nT/√Hz, a pixel dwell time under 1 ms, and a spatial resolution of 1.6 μm, allowing full-field images to be acquired within seconds.
conclusion: This technique enables quasi-real-time, non-invasive diagnostics of dynamic microwave devices and integrated circuits.

title: Quantum Lower Bounds For Convex Optimization And Real Matrix-vector Query Problems
abstract: ArXiv:2609.05679v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We (the author and the AI systems that did the heavy lifting) show that the quantum query complexity of minimizing a convex function over a convex subset of [MATH] with evaluation and membership queries is [MATH], nearly matching the best known upper bound. In particular, we show this even for quadratic minimization, which is equivalent to inverting an [MATH] real matrix using matrix-vector queries. We also show linear or nearly linear lower bounds on the quantum query complexity of computing the trace, the sign of the determinant, and the magnitude of the determinant of a real matrix in the matrix-vector query model. We use a novel quantum lower bound technique, the determinantal witness method, based on identifying a witness whose Fourier transform vanishes on low-rank matrices and that correlates well with the function being computed.
tldr: The paper proves quantum query complexity lower bounds for convex function minimization and real matrix-vector problems using a novel determinantal witness method.
motivation: To establish tight quantum lower bounds for convex optimization and matrix problems, nearly matching known upper bounds.
method: Introduces the determinantal witness method, which uses a witness whose Fourier transform vanishes on low-rank matrices and correlates with the function.
result: Shows nearly optimal lower bounds for quadratic minimization and linear or nearly linear lower bounds for computing trace and determinant properties.
conclusion: Provides a new technique for quantum query lower bounds and resolves complexity gaps for these problems.

title: multi-Stochastic Core Architecture For Scaling Probabilistic Ising Machines
authors: Chirag Garg, Pratik Brahma, Saavan Patel, Sayeef Salahuddin
abstract: ArXiv:2609.06365v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Ising Machines offer vast potential to solve NP-hard optimization problems efficiently that are intractable to solve using conventional computing architecture. A lot of these optimization problems fall into statistical learnability and involve finding an optimal solution among many possible, near-analogous configurations, by searching in a non-convex energy landscape. In this context, the probabilistic Boltzmann machine architecture especially PASS (Parallel Asynchronous Stochastic Sampler), explores and models the complex probability landscape pertaining to all possible configurations and excels in finding the ground-state energy solution of these intractable problems. Additionally, the noise-based neuron architecture addresses the limitation of conventional annealing methods, which may get stuck around local minima. Here, we demonstrate a stochastic sampling approach based on Block Gibbs Sampling to integrate multiple asynchronous PASS chips (four in this work), enabling improved scalability. Further, we demonstrate the scaling by mapping 784 nodes Max-Cut problem integrating 256 nodes PASS accelerator manufactured in 14 nm CMOS FinFET technology. PASS-enabled system with Block Gibbs Sampling protocol shows approximately 1000 times speedup for Max-Cut optimization compared to state-of-the-art methods implemented on CPUs and GPUs. The general applicability of this approach is further illustrated by solving a quantum spin chain Transverse Ising system and accurately representing complex probability landscapes. Moreover, our results demonstrate the change in the scaling law to constant in the scaled-PASS accelerator as compared to exponential on GPUs enabling at least 4 orders of magnitude improvement in time-to-solution. Hence, the presented methodology enables the pathway for scaling of asynchronous brain-like dynamics systems that do not follow any clock for its operation.
tldr: This paper demonstrates scaling of probabilistic Ising machines by integrating multiple PASS chips via Block Gibbs Sampling, achieving ~1000x speedup for Max-Cut problems.
motivation: To overcome scalability limitations of single Ising machine chips and provide efficient solutions to NP-hard optimization problems.
method: They combine four asynchronous PASS chips using Block Gibbs Sampling, mapping a 784-node Max-Cut problem onto a 256-node accelerator.
result: The scaled system achieves ~1000x faster Max-Cut optimization than CPU/GPU implementations and shows constant scaling law with over 4 orders of magnitude improvement in time-to-solution.
conclusion: The architecture enables scalable asynchronous stochastic systems and offers a practical path for large-scale probabilistic computing.

title: Role Differentiation As Ignition Of A Collective Information Engine
abstract: ArXiv:2609.05442v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Informational active matter research has shown how measurement-informed decisions produce collective order, so far in systems that reach consensus. We identify a collective information engine that orders by differentiation instead, and construct a minimal instance using anti-coordination games, the simplest game class in which differentiated role information has value. Agents infer their role from a noisy social signal, and role-following action feeds back into that signal, shaping the incentive to follow roles. The schemas prescribing roles are themselves dynamic: resources accrued through coordinated role-play combine with population variability to shape and reinforce the schemas that generated them. The model thereby operationalizes Sewell's duality of schemas and resources, the influential but hitherto qualitative resolution of sociology's structure--agency debate. The engine ignites when a loop gain [MATH]---the product of identity persistence, cognitive capacity, and social feedback channel fidelity---exceeds one. For a schema repertoire, roles emerge in a bifurcation cascade whose functional form is fixed by the repertoire's eigenvalue spectrum, ranging from monitorable logarithmic sequences to deceptive spike-then-avalanche onsets. Resource accumulation turns schema competition into a replicator dynamics that selects the cascade type endogenously. Subcritical behavioral covariance reveals that type before onset, enabling early detection, and feedback channel parameters bias which type is selected. For agents interacting on a platform, adaptive platform design then becomes a control lever to throttle emergent coordination, e.g. for mitigating risks from distributional AI. Joining game theory, collective dynamics, and information engines, we open a route to an information thermodynamics of agent.
tldr: This paper proposes a collective information engine based on role differentiation in anti-coordination games, linking game theory, active matter, and thermodynamics but in a classical, non-quantum context.
motivation: To extend informational active matter research from consensus to differentiation as a source of collective order, and to operationalize the sociology concept of schema-resource duality.
method: The authors model agents that infer roles from noisy social signals and act accordingly, with feedback into the signal; they analyze the dynamics via loop gain, bifurcation cascades, and replicator dynamics.
result: The engine ignites when loop gain exceeds one, producing role emergence through a bifurcation cascade whose type depends on the schema repertoire's eigenvalue spectrum; resource accumulation drives schema competition.
conclusion: The work offers a control lever for managing emergent coordination on digital platforms, but it does not address quantum systems or align with the specified research directions.

title: Lee-Yang Zeros Of Modulated Xy Spin Chains With Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya Interaction: Zero-contour Topology And Quantum Phase-diagram Reconstruction
authors: Hong Jiang, Xiang-Ping Jiang, Yan-Chao Li
abstract: ArXiv:2609.05469v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate the Lee--Yang zeros (LYZ) of inhomogeneous anisotropic XY spin chains with Dzyaloshinskii--Moriya (DM) interactions in the complex transverse-field plane, focusing on their fundamental connection to quantum phase transitions. We systematically study uniform chains, period-2 and period-3 modulated chains, and Fibonacci quasiperiodic chains of lengths 5 and 8. As the DM coupling strength [MATH] increases, the LYZ exhibit qualitatively distinct topological evolutions on the complex plane: the complex zeros of the uniform chain collapse toward the real axis; periodic chains feature either bifurcation of closed zero contours before all zeros become real or a single re-emergence of complex zeros; quasiperiodic chains exhibit repeated annihilation and revival of complex zeros. Analytical derivations demonstrate that this diverse behavior originates from DM-induced shifts of folded bands and the modulation of zero positions by anisotropic pairing at particle--hole band crossings. Our results establish a direct correspondence between LYZ topology and band deformation: isolated contact points of zeros with the real axis correspond to discrete quantum critical fields, while continuous real-zero intervals directly identify gapless chiral phases. Accordingly, beyond locating phase boundaries, LYZ can distinguish characteristic phases and serve as an intuitive probe for band folding and phase diagram restructuring.
tldr: The paper studies the topological evolution of Lee-Yang zeros in modulated XY spin chains with DM interaction, showing that their complex-plane behavior can identify quantum phase transitions and band deformations.
motivation: To understand the connection between Lee-Yang zeros and quantum phase transitions, and to use zero topology as a probe for phase diagrams in modulated spin chains.
method: Numerical and analytical study of XY spin chains with DM interaction, considering different modulation patterns (uniform, periodic, quasiperiodic) and examining the zeros of the partition function in the complex field plane.
result: The zeros exhibit distinct topological evolutions (collapse, bifurcation, annihilation/revival) depending on DM coupling and modulation, which are related to band structure and phase transitions.
conclusion: Lee-Yang zeros can serve as an intuitive probe for band folding and phase diagram restructuring, and can distinguish characteristic phases beyond locating phase boundaries.

title: Can A Local Quantum-Mechanical Description Of Physical Reality Be Considered Complete?
abstract: ArXiv:2609.05478v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In a complete quantum theory, one would construct it based on what we can observe in a system and operationally define in our universe. This philosophy goes back to some of the original ideals of quantum theory defined by W. Heisenberg, N. Bohr, and others as part of the Copenhagen school of thought. We argue in this letter that that if one wishes to construct a complete quantum field theory, that it is most natural to construct it based on a nonlocal theory of observable principles. If this interpretation is valid, then the one-particle nonrelativistic limit that recovers quantum mechanics would as well be nonlocal. In this interpretation we derive the nonlocal Schr\"odinger equation. We will as well demonstrate that the canonical position--momentum commutator and the Heisenberg uncertainty principle emerge from translation covariance.
tldr: 该论文试图基于非局域观测原理构建一个完整的量子场论，并推导出非局域的薛定谔方程。
motivation: 作者认为，基于可观测原理构建完整的量子理论是自然的，并假设这种理论本质上是非局域的。
method: 通过形式推导，从非局域前提导出非局域薛定谔方程，并证明位置-动量对易关系和不确定性关系可从平移协变性中涌现。
result: 展示了非局域量子描述能够自然地重现量子力学的基本结构，如非局域波方程和基本对易关系。
conclusion: 作者认为非局域解释可能为构造完整的量子场论和量子力学提供更基础的视角。

title: "It's Getting Away From Us!" - Black Hole Horizons And Relative Speed
abstract: ArXiv:2609.05524v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Black holes hold considerable fascination for the general public and students alike, and are commonly included in general-science courses on astronomy or modern physics. But teaching about the basics of black holes poses a considerable challenge: Any rigorous description requires concepts and techniques from general relativity, Einstein's theory of geometry and gravitation. And any half-way rigorous introduction to that theory, including the required mathematical tools, is significantly beyond the level of general-science courses. Inevitably, accounts of relativistic physics at the introductory undergraduate level make use of analogies, approximations and simplified models to teach about topics like black holes, gravitational waves, gravitational lensing, or cosmology. The purpose of this article is to given an account of one particular set of analogies for teaching about black holes, all of which are based on modelling the motions of observers in the vicinity of the black hole and rely on the concept of (relative) speed to describe properties of the black hole. While most elements of what I am about to describe can be found in the existing literature, I am not aware of any text that attempts to pull them together into a unified picture at a suitable level of presentation for undergraduate-level teaching; that is the goal of the present text.
tldr: This paper presents educational analogies for teaching black hole concepts using relative speed, aimed at undergraduate general science courses.
motivation: Teaching black holes rigorously requires general relativity, which is beyond introductory courses; hence analogies are needed.
method: The author collects and unifies various analogies that model observer motion near black holes using relative speed.
result: Provides a unified set of analogies at a suitable level for undergraduate teaching.
conclusion: Aims to improve teaching of black hole concepts by offering an accessible approach.

title: $N$-dimensional Discrete Fourier Transform Via Bosonic Hamiltonian
authors: Edgar Barriga, Camila Mu\~noz, Alejandro Mu\~noz, Santiago Rojas-Rojas, Pablo Solano, Carla Hermann-Avigliano, Aldo Delgado
abstract: ArXiv:2609.05644v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The discrete Fourier transform (DFT) underpins many classical algorithms and is a fundamental unitary operator for quantum information processing. Implementing the [MATH]-dimensional DFT in photonic integrated circuits (PICs) is limited by the cascades of Mach-Zehnder interferometers that current architectures require. Here we propose bosonic Hamiltonians that realize the [MATH]-dimensional DFT through a single stage of multimode evolution, complemented only by phase shifters before and after the interaction region, in a geometry suited to 3D waveguides. Modeling the system as a graph, where edges correspond to couplings and the vertices are the waveguides, we obtain analytical solutions for complete graphs up to [MATH] and numerical solutions up to [MATH]. For non-complete graphs, different propagation constants are required in the Hamiltonian. We report all solutions for [MATH], partial exploration for [MATH], and selected cases for [MATH], together with three conjectures that guide the numerical search for [MATH]. These configurations circumvent the vanishing evanescent coupling strength imposed by the waveguide separation, and a closed-form sensitivity criterion selects those that are admissible as a waveguide layout and least sensitive to fabrication error. We also uncover the missing non-affine parameters of the [MATH]-dimensional DFT, and show that the scaling law for implementing the [MATH]-dimensional DFT with our building blocks is [MATH]. This allows assembling the [MATH]-dimensional DFT with only [MATH] interferometers, in contrast to the [MATH] of Reck and Clements architectures.
tldr: This paper proposes bosonic Hamiltonians to implement the N-dimensional discrete Fourier transform in photonic integrated circuits using fewer interferometers than traditional architectures.
motivation: The discrete Fourier transform is fundamental for quantum information processing, but current photonic implementations require cascades of Mach-Zehnder interferometers, limiting scalability.
method: The authors model the photonic circuit as a graph, deriving analytical solutions for complete graphs up to N and numerical solutions for larger N, and propose a scaling law for implementation.
result: They report configurations that circumvent evanescent coupling limitations and achieve the N-dimensional DFT with only O(log N) interferometers, contrasting with the O(N^2) of Reck and Clements architectures.
conclusion: This work offers a more efficient photonic implementation of the DFT, potentially advancing quantum computing hardware, but it is not aligned with the specific theoretical or networking interests of the user.

title: Kerr Induced Control Of Synchronization And Quantum State Recovery In A Driven Van Der Pol Oscillator
authors: Amir Hossein Houshmand Almani, Ali Mortezapour, Alireza Nourmandipour
abstract: ArXiv:2609.05672v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate how Kerr nonlinearity modifies quantum synchronization in a squeezed quantum van der Pol oscillator. We show that the Kerr interaction produces an amplitude-dependent frequency shift that drives a saddle-node bifurcation, transforming the classical phase-space structure from bistable to monostable dynamics. In the quantum regime, this transition manifests as systematic frequency pulling and spectral broadening, while the steady-state Wigner function reveals a continuous correspondence between the quantum state and the semiclassical attractor despite finite quantum fluctuations. By constructing global synchronization phase diagrams in the squeezing--Kerr parameter space, we uncover a remarkably linear dependence of the critical squeezing strength required to maintain phase locking on the Kerr nonlinearity. We further demonstrate that the synchronization boundary does not coincide with the crossover between super- and sub-Poissonian photon statistics, showing that synchronization and photon-number statistics characterize distinct aspects of the quantum steady state. These results provide quantitative design principles for controlling quantum synchronization through Kerr nonlinearity, with potential relevance to trapped-ion, superconducting-circuit, and optomechanical platforms.
tldr: This paper studies the effect of Kerr nonlinearity on quantum synchronization in a driven van der Pol oscillator, showing how it induces transitions and controls phase locking.
motivation: To understand and control quantum synchronization, which is important for quantum technologies, by using Kerr nonlinearity as a tunable parameter.
method: Using a master equation approach and semiclassical analysis, the authors analyze the steady-state dynamics, Wigner function, and synchronization measures.
result: They find that Kerr nonlinearity causes a saddle-node bifurcation converting bistable to monostable dynamics, and that the critical squeezing for synchronization scales linearly with Kerr strength.
conclusion: The results offer design principles for controlling quantum synchronization via Kerr nonlinearity, relevant to various quantum platforms.

title: Physical Policy Gradient Theorem For In Situ Stochastic-adjoint Training
abstract: ArXiv:2609.05808v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In situ adjoint training extracts parameter gradients directly from measurement, but has so far been limited to reciprocal or restricted systems. Here, we introduce the physical counterpart of the policy gradient theorem: a stochastic-adjoint gradient estimator that lifts these constraints by trading reciprocity for nondegenerate diffusion. As validation, we train a nonlinear resonator network, whose own dynamics supply the policy, against antagonistic temporal modulations with gradients from measured stochastic trajectories alone, without finite differences or a separate adjoint experiment.
tldr: This paper introduces a stochastic-adjoint gradient estimator inspired by the policy gradient theorem for in situ training of physical systems, demonstrated on a nonlinear resonator network.
motivation: In situ adjoint training is limited to reciprocal or restricted systems, so the authors aim to lift these constraints to enable broader physical training.
method: The proposed method trades reciprocity for nondegenerate diffusion to construct a stochastic-adjoint estimator that extracts gradients directly from measured stochastic trajectories.
result: Validation shows successful training of a nonlinear resonator network against antagonistic temporal modulations using only measured data, without finite differences or separate adjoint experiments.
conclusion: The method expands the applicability of in situ training to non-reciprocal and complex physical systems, opening new avenues for physical learning.

title: Topologically Protected Edge States In One-Dimensional Quantum Walks
authors: Emily Maxey, Jacob Mansfield, Beth Thacker, Wade Degottardi
abstract: ArXiv:2609.05823v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Topological insulators host protected boundary states that are robust to disorder, making them attractive for applications and motivating their realization in engineered systems. Discrete-time quantum walks, which have been implemented in a variety of experimental platforms, can exhibit topologically nontrivial phases and their associated boundary states. Here, we introduce a class of topological quantum walks with variable step lengths that offer theoretical insights into the topological classification of such walks. For example, these walks can access higher winding numbers and support multiple edge states. They also provide context for the reduction of topological protection from a [MATH]- to [MATH]-valued invariant when time-reversal symmetry is broken. The topologically protected edge states are investigated using a transfer-matrix approach that describes their spatial profiles and spin structures. These predictions are in excellent agreement with numerical results and, where applicable, with the Jackiw--Rebbi zero-mode solution of the Dirac equation. Taken together, our analysis provides a roadmap for designing quantum walks with control over the number, spatial profile, and spin structure of their topological edge states.
tldr: This paper explores topological edge states in one-dimensional quantum walks with variable step lengths, showing how to control the number and structure of these states.
motivation: Topological insulators host protected boundary states robust to disorder, motivating their realization in engineered systems like quantum walks for potential applications in quantum information processing.
method: The authors introduce a class of topological quantum walks with variable step lengths and analyze the edge states using a transfer-matrix approach, comparing with Jackiw-Rebbi solutions.
result: These walks can achieve higher winding numbers and support multiple edge states, with spatial profiles and spin structures accurately predicted by the transfer-matrix method.
conclusion: The analysis provides a roadmap for designing quantum walks with controllable topological edge states, but the work is primarily focused on condensed-matter analogies rather than quantum information applications.

title: On The Sample Complexity Of The Generalized Hidden Shift Problem Over Arbitrary Finite Groups
abstract: ArXiv:2609.05828v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We formulate the generalized hidden shift problem over arbitrary finite groups and obtain upper and lower bounds for the sample complexity in terms of group theoretic data.
tldr: The paper formulates the generalized hidden shift problem over arbitrary finite groups and establishes upper and lower bounds on sample complexity in terms of group-theoretic data.
motivation: To understand how the sample complexity of hidden shift problems depends on the underlying group structure, and to provide bounds for arbitrary finite groups.
method: The authors define a generalized version of the hidden shift problem for arbitrary finite groups and analyze sample complexity using group-theoretic properties.
result: They obtain both upper and lower bounds for the sample complexity, expressed in terms of group invariants.
conclusion: The bounds characterize the minimal number of samples needed to solve the problem, linking it to group-theoretic data.

title: High-Resolution Dynamical Eigenspectroscopy Via Variational Trotter Compression On A Superconducting Qubit Processor
authors: Liyang Sui, Xingrui Liu, Yufan Li, Sainan Huai, Zhiwen Zong, Kunliang Bu, Xiaopei Yang, Wenyan Jin, Bowen Chen, Xutao Zhang, Jianlan Wu, Shengyu Zhang, Yi Yin
abstract: ArXiv:2609.05838v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The pursuit of high-resolution eigenspectroscopy on noisy intermediate-scale quantum devices is often hindered by the trade-off between circuit depth and coherence time. In this work, we introduce and experimentally demonstrate a dynamical eigenspectroscopy protocol that extracts fine-grained energy structures from time-dependent survival amplitudes. To overcome the finite coherence window of current superconducting processors, we employ Variational Trotter Compression (VTC) as a practical means to extend the duration of high-fidelity unitary evolution. Using a multi-connected 9-qubit superconducting processor, we reconstruct the time-domain autocorrelation signal via quantum state tomography for the H2 molecule at different bond lengths and for the Fermi-Hubbard model across different correlation regimes. Through multi-frequency fitting and Fourier analysis, the extracted eigenenergies agree with the exact-diagonalization values to within 2x10^-3, including the near-degenerate levels in the strongly interacting regime. Our results establish experimental dynamical spectroscopy as a robust and generalizable framework for simulating both quantum chemistry and strongly correlated lattice systems, bridging weak- and strong-coupling regimes on near-term quantum hardware.
tldr: This paper introduces a dynamical eigenspectroscopy protocol using variational Trotter compression on a superconducting qubit processor to extract fine-grained energy structures with high precision.
motivation: To overcome the trade-off between circuit depth and coherence time in noisy intermediate-scale quantum devices, enabling high-resolution energy spectroscopy.
method: The authors employ Variational Trotter Compression to extend high-fidelity evolution, then reconstruct time-domain autocorrelation signals via quantum state tomography on a 9-qubit processor, followed by multi-frequency fitting and Fourier analysis.
result: Extracted eigenenergies agree with exact diagonalization to within 2×10^-3, including near-degenerate levels, for H2 and Fermi-Hubbard models across different correlation regimes.
conclusion: This work establishes experimental dynamical spectroscopy as a robust and generalizable framework for simulating quantum chemistry and strongly correlated lattice systems on near-term quantum hardware.

title: Do Quantum AIs Dream In Paths? Path-Integral Slow Thinking Through Grover Interference
authors: Xiansheng Cai, Xiu-Hao Deng, Kun Chen
abstract: ArXiv:2609.05842v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards enables large language models to think slowly, but the same training can induce policy collapse: probability concentrates onto a few successful trajectories and exploratory diversity erodes. We ask whether quantum AI can realize slow thinking differently. We formulate slow thinking as coherent dynamics over reasoning trajectories, a discrete path integral in which action sequences coexist in superposition and recombine before measurement. In our trainable realization, an exact verifier partitions the ensemble into collective accepted and rejected components that interfere under Grover amplitude amplification. A finite Grover evolution is maximized when the pre-amplification success probability lies at an analytically determined value below one, so inference itself defines an interior training target and removes the monotonic pressure toward unit success. In exact statevector simulations of a 2x3 sliding puzzle, Grover training reaches accuracy 0.95 on a 32-question training set at one round, against 0.73 for the strongest classical control. On held-out questions specialization has a cost: an untrained uniform policy read out through the same amplification remains the strongest reference on this solution-dense benchmark, and quantum training preserves far more held-out accuracy than classical training - at four rounds with matched circuit applications the two quantum models reach 3.2 and 3.9 times the strongest classical controls. The number of training questions supported by fixed-size policies trained at each amplification budget also grows faster with the budget than with matched classical repetition. These results establish a Grover-based realization of path-integral slow thinking: the interior target preserves exploratory path diversity, and ensemble-level interference converts it into verified performance.
tldr: This paper proposes a Grover-amplification-based path-integral approach to 'slow thinking' in quantum AI, treating reasoning trajectories as superposed paths and using interference to preserve diversity while achieving high accuracy.
motivation: Classical reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards causes policy collapse, concentrating probability onto few successful trajectories and eroding exploratory diversity. The authors ask whether quantum AI can implement slow thinking differently, avoiding this monotonic pressure toward unit success.
method: They formulate slow thinking as coherent dynamics over a discrete path integral of action sequences, and train a model using Grover amplitude amplification to interfere between accepted and rejected components, with an analytically derived interior success probability as the training target.
result: Exact statevector simulations on a 2x3 sliding puzzle show that Grover training achieves 0.95 accuracy on a 32-question training set versus 0.73 for the strongest classical control, and preserves far more held-out accuracy (3.2x and 3.9x better at matched circuit applications).
conclusion: The results establish a Grover-based realization of path-integral slow thinking, where the interior target preserves exploratory path diversity and ensemble-level interference converts it into verified performance.

title: Demailly's Conjecture In Quantum Language And Its Solution
abstract: ArXiv:2609.05866v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We give an exact translation between fat-point interpolation in complex projective space and a dark-state problem for fixed-particle-number bosons. Under the unitary Fischer--Bargmann realization, homogeneous degree becomes particle number, the Veronese lift becomes a bosonic symmetric product state, and order-[MATH] vanishing becomes orthogonality to all coherent jet excitations of orders below [MATH]. The initial degree of a symbolic power is therefore the first particle number admitting a dark state of a positive constraint Hamiltonian, and the Waldschmidt constant is the asymptotic particle cost per suppression order. After developing both sides of this dictionary from first principles, we prove a finite-scale no-dark-state amplification theorem. Frobenius amplifies the associated full-rank certificate in one good positive-characteristic fiber; a nonzero maximal minor returns it to characteristic zero. Its asymptotic consequence is Demailly's conjectured inequality. The paper is written so that the projective statement, the quantum reformulation, and the arithmetic part of the solution can be read independently and then identified exactly.

motivation: The paper aims to bridge complex projective geometry and quantum many-body physics, potentially offering new insights into both fields.
method: The authors establish a dictionary between fat-point interpolation and bosonic dark states, then use arithmetic tools like Frobenius amplification to prove the conjecture.
result: They prove Demailly's conjectured inequality, demonstrating the equivalence between the geometric and quantum formulations.
conclusion: The paper is a mathematical result with quantum language, but it is not directly applicable to the user's research areas in quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid systems.

title: Boundary-Cancelled Score-Hamiltonian Sampling
abstract: ArXiv:2609.05904v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Diffusion sampling can be viewed as imaginary-time annealing of probability densities. From a forward/backward Euclidean Schr\"odinger pair, we show that fixing the noising drift forces the reverse score term, and that the same logarithmic force is the one-sided imaginary-time counterdiabatic connection of a supersymmetric Score Hamiltonian. The correspondence turns score-learning error into a Hamiltonian perturbation and yields a schedule principle: if the first [MATH] terminal derivatives vanish, Morita--Nishimori boundary cancellation suppresses the residual Hellinger error from [MATH] to [MATH] until score or sampling floors are reached. Reverse-SDE benchmarks, including two-dimensional learned-score tests, confirm the predicted improvement.

motivation: To improve the efficiency and accuracy of diffusion sampling methods, which are widely used in generative modeling, by drawing on quantum-inspired concepts like counterdiabatic driving and supersymmetry to guide the sampling schedule.
method: The authors establish a formal correspondence between diffusion sampling and a supersymmetric Score Hamiltonian, showing that fixing the noising drift determines the reverse score term and that score-learning errors act as Hamiltonian perturbations. They then derive a schedule principle based on boundary cancellation conditions when initial terminal derivatives vanish.

conclusion: The quantum-inspired framework provides a principled method for designing sampling schedules that achieve near-optimal performance until inherent score or sampling floors are reached, highlighting the utility of quantum concepts in classical machine learning tasks.

title: Reducing Quantum And Classical Resources For Quantum-centric Supercomputing Workloads On Near-term Hardware
authors: Maxence Grandadam, Vladyslav Bohun, Dikshant Dulal, Maciej Koch-Janusz
abstract: ArXiv:2609.05957v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Sample-based Krylov quantum diagonalization (SKQD) is a paradigmatic example of a quantum-centric supercomputing workflow that combines the convergence structure of Krylov quantum diagonalization with classical sampling-based post-processing. It provides convergence guarantees assuming that the important computational-basis configurations can be sampled from a set of Krylov states with sufficient probability. We analyze this assumption under depolarizing noise, deriving shot-count resource estimates that expose an exponential depth penalty, and perform experiments on current noisy hardware with the one-dimensional single-impurity Anderson model on a 20-site (40-qubit) instance. Device noise breaks the practical convergence predicted by the noiseless SKQD analysis, but approximate compilation techniques can compress the Krylov time-evolution circuits before execution. The compressed circuits accumulate less hardware noise, recover the expected energy convergence, and reduce both the quantum shot budget and the classical subspace dimension, remaining beneficial even when classical configuration recovery is applied.
tldr: The paper analyzes sample-based Krylov quantum diagonalization under depolarizing noise and shows that approximate compilation can reduce quantum and classical resources on near-term hardware.
motivation: To make quantum-centric supercomputing workflows feasible on noisy hardware by minimizing both quantum and classical resource requirements.
method: The authors derive shot-count estimates under depolarizing noise, revealing an exponential depth penalty, and then apply approximate compilation to compress the Krylov time-evolution circuits.
result: Experiments on a 40-qubit Anderson model demonstrate that circuit compression reduces hardware noise, recovers energy convergence, and lowers both the quantum shot budget and the classical subspace dimension.
conclusion: Approximate compilation is an effective technique to mitigate noise and improve the practicality of sample-based Krylov quantum diagonalization on near-term quantum devices.

title: Motion-Tracking Terahertz Time-Domain Spectroscopy Enabled By Time-Programmable Frequency Combs For Moving-Object Sensing
authors: Riku Shibata, Shun Fujii, Tomofumi Ikari, Shinichi Watanabe
abstract: ArXiv:2609.06024v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Terahertz time-domain spectroscopy (THz-TDS) provides direct access to both spectral information and time-of-flight features, making it attractive for dynamic sensing. However, conventional high-speed THz-TDS methods typically rely on a fixed delay trajectory, limiting their ability to selectively acquire only the relevant temporal window while tracking target motion. Here, we demonstrate motion-tracking THz-TDS based on time-programmable frequency combs (TPFCs), in which the THz measurement window is actively locked to a moving time-domain waveform. By continuously modulating the phase-lock set point of one TPFC, we perform real-time apodized acquisition of a specific temporal window centered on the main THz peak at rates up to 308 Hz. Simultaneously, the residual peak position within the window is detected in real time and fed back to the other comb, enabling the measurement window to follow target displacements exceeding the original acquisition window. The feedback command together with the residual peak position further enables reconstruction of the relative target displacement. As a proof-of-concept demonstration, we use a moving gold mirror to simulate respiration- and heartbeat-related motion superimposed on a much larger displacement representing body motion, and successfully resolve the two vital-sign-related components from the measured displacement. This work extends arbitrary-delay control with TPFCs to THz-TDS and establishes a motion-compensated spectroscopy platform for simultaneous displacement tracking and THz waveform acquisition.
tldr: This paper demonstrates motion-tracking terahertz time-domain spectroscopy using time-programmable frequency combs to lock the measurement window to a moving target, enabling simultaneous displacement tracking and waveform acquisition.
motivation: Conventional high-speed THz-TDS uses a fixed delay trajectory, which limits selective temporal window acquisition while tracking moving objects. The authors aim to overcome this limitation.
method: Two time-programmable frequency combs are used: one comb's phase-lock set point is modulated to perform real-time apodized acquisition at up to 308 Hz, and the residual peak position is fed back to the other comb to follow large target displacements.
result: Proof-of-concept with a moving gold mirror simulating respiration and heartbeat motions on a larger body movement successfully resolved both vital-sign components from the measured displacement.
conclusion: The work establishes a motion-compensated THz-TDS platform that extends arbitrary-delay control with TPFCs, enabling simultaneous displacement tracking and THz waveform acquisition.

title: A Power Geometry And Hypergeometric Functions
abstract: ArXiv:2609.05474v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper is a corrected English translation of an original Japanese work introducing "power geometry," a research programme centred on power transformations, deformations and dualities of functions in the sense of optimisation theory. Its two main motivations are the origin of probability distributions (via maximum-likelihood principles, rational-function parameters and ODEs linked to information geometry, the Pearson system and Schwarzian equations) and the construction of matrix dynamical systems that compute eigenvalues, singular values and principal or minor subspaces. Building on Brockett's double-bracket flows, the author extends these systems to rectangular matrices, flag manifolds and difference-of-convex potentials, and shows how a continuous power parameter can interpolate between largest- and smallest-eigenvalue problems. Dual potentials, topological distinctions between principal and minor subspace flows, and links via matrix Schwarzian--Riccati equations are examined, with a view toward design principles for classical and quantum information-processing algorithms.
tldr: Introduces power geometry as a research programme linking probability distributions and matrix dynamical systems via power transformations and dualities.
motivation: To explore the origins of probability distributions through maximum-likelihood principles and to construct matrix dynamical systems that compute eigenvalues and subspaces.
method: Builds on Brockett's double-bracket flows, extending them to rectangular matrices and flag manifolds, and introduces a continuous power parameter for interpolation.
result: Examines dual potentials, topological aspects of flows, and connections via matrix Schwarzian–Riccati equations, proposing design principles for information-processing algorithms.
conclusion: The paper presents a mathematical framework potentially applicable to classical and quantum information processing, but it is not directly aligned with the specified research directions.

title: Third-order Relativistic Kinematics And Siacci Shock Decompositions Via Localised Darboux Frames
abstract: ArXiv:2609.05497v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Constrained particle trajectories along lower-dimensional world sheets constitute a foundational domain in relativistic kinematics and submanifold theory. This paper establishes a comprehensive geometric and kinematic framework for third-order particle dynamics constrained to timelike surfaces in Minkowski 3-space. By utilising the localised Darboux frame, we explicitly derive the relativistically invariant parameters, namely the geodesic curvature, normal curvature, and geodesic torsion and analyse the non-linear coupling between the intrinsic surface topology and the extrinsic spacetime geometry. Primary focus is dedicated to formulating the relativistic "jerk" vector, which accounts for the instantaneous time rate of change of acceleration and captures the high-order structural stresses of the motion. Furthermore, we generalise Siacci's theorem to this Lorentzian setting, providing a non-perpendicular geometric decomposition of both the acceleration and jerk fields into explicit tangential and radial components relative to a fixed coordinate origin. Our formulations explicitly unveil the hidden central-force dynamics and dimensional compactification mechanisms under planar constraints, showing that out-of-plane torsional shocks vanish identically when the modified geodesic torsion is suppressed. These results offer novel analytical insights for structural stability and conserved angular momentum-like quantities governing constrained physical systems in non-Euclidean spacetimes.
tldr: This paper develops a geometric framework for third-order particle dynamics on timelike surfaces in Minkowski 3-space using Darboux frames, generalizing Siacci's theorem to a Lorentzian setting.
motivation: To understand higher-order structural stresses and hidden central-force dynamics in constrained relativistic motion, which may offer insights into structural stability and conserved quantities in non-Euclidean spacetimes.
method: The paper uses localized Darboux frames to derive relativistically invariant parameters (geodesic curvature, normal curvature, geodesic torsion) and formulates a relativistic jerk vector. It then generalizes Siacci's theorem to provide a non-perpendicular decomposition of acceleration and jerk into tangential and radial components.
result: The decomposition explicitly reveals hidden central-force dynamics and dimensional compactification mechanisms under planar constraints, showing that out-of-plane torsional shocks vanish when the modified geodesic torsion is suppressed.
conclusion: The results provide novel analytical insights for structural stability and conserved angular momentum-like quantities in constrained physical systems in non-Euclidean spacetimes.

title: Schwarz-Type Null Curves In $\mathbb{C}^4$: Symmetry And Period Reduction

title: Trihexagonal Magic Figures: A High-Constraint-Density Triangular Combinatorial Design And The Possibility Of A Phase Transition

title: Recursive Overlap Bernoulli Distributions And An Entropy Concavity Conjecture
abstract: ArXiv:2609.05546v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce a family of recursively generated finite probability distributions obtained from left and right embeddings with overlaps. The conjecture is proved in the two extremal cases and supported by symbolic computations for numerous overlap sequences.

motivation: Explores distributions interpolating between binomial and non-overlapping Bernoulli products, and analyzes the concavity of their entropy.
method: Defines recursive embeddings with overlaps, derives formulas for moments, and uses symbolic computations to support the entropy concavity conjecture.
