The discontinuous structure yields an exact element-local sampler for the restricted white noise. Numerical experiments on irregular polygonal, non-convex polytopic and reentrant domains support the predicted convergence behaviour.
tldr: The paper presents a numerical analysis of discontinuous Galerkin methods for elliptic SPDEs driven by spatial white noise on polytopic meshes, proving sharp convergence rates.
motivation: To develop and analyze numerical approximations for elliptic stochastic partial differential equations with low-regularity solutions induced by white noise, while handling complex polytopic mesh geometries.
method: The authors restrict the white-noise functional to the discontinuous polynomial space and split the error into stochastic forcing-restriction and deterministic discretization components, employing symmetric interior-penalty discontinuous Galerkin methods.
result: Sharp two-sided error estimates are proven for fixed polynomial degree, showing rates of h^{2-d/2} in L^2 norm, with optimality established via finite-dimensional lower bounds and support for non-convex and reentrant polytopic elements.
conclusion: The proposed approach achieves optimal stochastic convergence despite low solution regularity and complex mesh geometries, validated by numerical experiments on irregular polygonal and non-convex domains.

title: Dynamical Systems And Nonconvex Quadratic Programs
abstract: ArXiv:2609.06088v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper studies a dynamical system approach for solving indefinite quadratic programming problems subject to linear constraints. We investigate the convergence of the trajectory generated by the system to a Karush-Kuhn-Tucker point of the quadratic programs. In addition, we derive an estimate for the distance between the trajectory and a solution of the problem. We further prove that the objective value is decreasing along the trajectory. An illustrative example and a numerical test are presented to demonstrate the behavior and performance of the proposed method.
tldr: This paper proposes a dynamical system approach for solving indefinite quadratic programming problems with linear constraints and analyzes its convergence properties.
motivation: The motivation is to tackle nonconvex quadratic programs, which are NP-hard in general, using continuous dynamical systems that can efficiently converge to stationary points.
method: The method models the optimization problem as a continuous-time dynamical system and studies the convergence of its trajectory to Karush-Kuhn-Tucker points, providing an estimate for the distance to an optimal solution.
result: The paper proves that the objective function decreases along the trajectory and provides convergence guarantees, along with an illustrative example and numerical test.
conclusion: The proposed dynamical system approach appears to be a viable method for solving certain nonconvex quadratic programs, demonstrating good performance in practice.

title: Three-sided Mobility-energy Market Design As A Multiperiod Stochastic Assignment Game
authors: Joseph Y. J. Chow Hai Yang
abstract: ArXiv:2609.05449v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: As mobility service providers (MSPs) and energy providers (EPs) expand electric vehicle ecosystems, models are needed to understand their interactions within a three-sided market. Existing frameworks often overlook the temporal interdependencies between mobility and charging demands. We address this gap by proposing a bilevel problem as an assignment game overseen by a market regulator. The upper level optimizes service pricing to maximize platform profitability. The lower level models a multi-stakeholder equilibrium using a scalable, link-based Perturbed Utility Route Choice (PURC) framework. The evaluation time frame is divided into discrete intervals, capturing the temporal lag between mobility and charging demand via an empirical affine function. We solve the model by chronologically decomposing the lower level into interacting mobility service and recharge subnetworks. Numerical experiments on the expanded Nguyen-Dupuis network reveal several key insights. First, a critical charging capacity threshold exists; operating below it forces a severe reduction in the deployable fleet and creates localized transit deserts. Second, modeling endogenous operating costs reveals a concave profit trajectory, demonstrating that total profit maximizes at a specific fleet size just before market saturation. Third, optimal dynamic pricing operates within a narrow range, where peak pricing acts as a steady revenue driver and off-peak pricing serves as a highly sensitive operational buffer. These findings provide actionable strategies for coordinating fleet sizing and charging infrastructure deployment.
tldr: This paper proposes a bilevel optimization model for a three-sided mobility-energy market, integrating pricing and fleet sizing decisions using a stochastic assignment game.
motivation: Existing frameworks overlook temporal interdependencies between mobility and charging demands in electric vehicle ecosystems, necessitating a coordinated market design.
method: They develop a bilevel assignment game with a market regulator, using a link-based Perturbed Utility Route Choice (PURC) framework for the lower level, and solve it via chronological decomposition into interacting mobility and recharge subnetworks.
result: Numerical experiments on the Nguyen-Dupuis network reveal a critical charging capacity threshold, a concave profit trajectory with respect to fleet size, and optimal dynamic pricing within a narrow range.
conclusion: The model provides actionable strategies for coordinating fleet sizing and charging infrastructure deployment in integrated mobility-energy systems.

title: A 1.283 Price-of-Anarchy Bound For The Repeated Virtual First-Price Auction
abstract: ArXiv:2609.05499v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the repeated allocation of a single indivisible resource among [MATH] strategic players. Each player [MATH] has a privately known value distribution [MATH], and values are drawn independently across players and periods. The goal is to find fair and efficient mechanisms. We apply the repeated first-price auction with equal initial endowments of virtual money. We show that each player can asymptotically secure the same fair-floor guarantee [MATH] as in Cs\'oka 2026; consequently, the mechanism is [MATH]-optimal. This provides a simpler and more robust alternative mechanism for this special case and may also help derive sharper upper bounds on the price of anarchy.
tldr: This paper studies repeated allocation of a single indivisible resource among strategic players using a repeated first-price auction with virtual money, showing it achieves a fair-floor guarantee and is optimal in terms of price of anarchy.
motivation: To find fair and efficient mechanisms for allocating a single resource over time when players have private valuations.
method: Applies a repeated first-price auction with equal initial endowments of virtual money, and analyzes its performance in terms of price of anarchy.
result: Shows each player can asymptotically secure the same fair-floor guarantee as in a previous work, making the mechanism optimal, and offers a simpler and more robust alternative.
conclusion: The proposed mechanism is a robust and optimal alternative for repeated allocation, potentially leading to sharper upper bounds on the price of anarchy.

title: Reaching The Cards Apple Wallet Leaves Behind: Direct Nfc Acquisition Of Pro100, Humo And Uzcard Payment Cards On iOS
abstract: ArXiv:2609.05627v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Contactless payment from a phone has become routine in many markets, but the convenience is unevenly distributed. Apple currently lists Kazakhstan among supported Apple Pay markets, but not Uzbekistan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan or Turkmenistan. In Uzbekistan, HUMO and UZCARD are the two national interbank retail card systems, and both include contactless card products. This paper describes an application-level card-capture method for tested PRO100, HUMO and UZCARD cards on NFC-capable iPhones. Using Core NFC, the reader opens a tag session, selects an application when necessary, and recovers the primary account number (PAN) and expiry date from the returned data. The difficult parts were empirical: identifying AIDs that worked on the tested cards and decoding card-generation-specific response layouts. The implementation was later hardened around a hybrid parsing path that prefers BER-TLV/EMV fields when present and keeps the observed offsets only as a legacy fallback. The paper also gives a system-level workflow, a threat model, explicit failure handling, a platform comparison, and a reproducible evaluation protocol. No claim is made that the same behavior is available unchanged on every iPhone/iOS combination, on iPadOS or macOS, or under future Core NFC policy. The method captures registration data; it does not emulate a card, authorize a payment, or treat an NFC read as proof of ownership.
tldr: A paper describing an NFC-based method to extract account numbers and expiry dates from contactless payment cards using an iPhone's Core NFC framework.
motivation: To investigate a potential security weakness in contactless payment cards by demonstrating that card data can be read without physical contact using an iPhone.
method: The author used Core NFC on an iPhone to open a tag session, identified application identifiers (AIDs) for PRO100, HUMO, and UZCARD cards, and decoded proprietary response layouts to extract the primary account number (PAN) and expiry date.
result: The method successfully recovered PAN and expiry data from all tested cards, with a hybrid parsing approach that handles both standard BER-TLV/EMV fields and legacy observed offsets.
conclusion: The paper highlights a practical data capture risk for certain contactless payment cards, although it does not enable payment authorization or card emulation, and emphasizes that the method's applicability varies across devices and iOS versions.

title: Xai-sdn: An Explainable Entropy-Guided Machine Learning Framework For Real-Time DDoS Detection In Software Defined Networks
authors: Adeel Ahmad, Ali Akarma, Ahmad Ali, Hammad Muneer, Toqeer Ali Syed
abstract: ArXiv:2609.05701v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: One of the biggest risks faced by Software Defined Networks (SDN) is the Distributed Denial of Service (DDoS) attack in which a compromised controller can make an entire network unusable. To address these challenges, we suggest an entropy-guided machine learning framework, called XAI-SDN, for real-time DDoS detection in SDN environments which is lightweight and explainable. The framework extends the flow features extracted by CICFlowMeter with eight Shannon entropy metrics obtained by an [MATH] rolling algorithm and uses a Random Forest classifier with SHAP TreeExplainer for providing transparency at the prediction level. On a fixed temporal split, XAI-SDN achieves an accuracy of 99.9987\%, a macro F1-score of 99.9621\%, and an AUC-ROC of 1.0000 on the full 3.59 million flows of the CIC-DDoS2019 SYN benchmark. The pipeline sustains 0.0165~ms per flow (60{,}606 flows/s) without the use of SHAP and 0.5122~ms per flow (1{,}953 flows/s) with full support of SHAP under the 99.14\% prevalence of DDoS traffic, which is a step towards achieving a balance between the detection performance and operational transparency in next-generation SDN security.
tldr: Proposes an explainable entropy-guided machine learning framework (XAI-SDN) for real-time DDoS detection in Software Defined Networks.
motivation: DDoS attacks can cripple SDN controllers; existing detection methods often lack lightweightness and explainability.
method: Extends CICFlowMeter features with eight Shannon entropy metrics using a rolling algorithm, applies Random Forest with SHAP TreeExplainer for transparent predictions.
result: Achieves 99.9987% accuracy, 99.9621% macro F1-score, and AUC-ROC 1.0 on CIC-DDoS2019 SYN dataset; processes 60,606 flows/s without SHAP and 1,953 flows/s with SHAP.
conclusion: The framework balances high detection performance with operational transparency, suitable for real-time SDN security.

title: Utility-Driven Spatial Data Sampling For UAV-Assisted Scientific Smart Farming
abstract: ArXiv:2609.05765v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large smart-farming deployments generate continuous scientific data from spatially distributed sensors, including soil, humidity, temperature, crop-health, and pest-related measurements. In vast agricultural fields, however, an energy-constrained unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) often cannot collect data from every sensor during each mission. Existing UAV-assisted collection methods typically optimize coverage, route length, data volume, or freshness, but they do not always distinguish between data that is merely available and data that is scientifically valuable. This poster introduces a utility-driven spatial sampling framework for UAV-assisted smart farming. The field is partitioned into grid cells, each sized according to the UAV ground coverage range. After an initial exploration phase, each cell receives a scientific utility score based on freshness, redundancy, anomaly likelihood, and model uncertainty. The UAV then selects and visits a subset of high-utility cells under battery and return-to-base constraints. The proposed framework reframes UAV-based collection as adaptive scientific data management rather than exhaustive sensing.
tldr: This paper introduces a utility-driven spatial sampling framework for UAV-assisted smart farming, where the UAV selects high-utility grid cells based on scientific value under battery constraints.
motivation: In large agricultural fields, a single energy-constrained UAV cannot collect data from every sensor, so it is important to prioritize sensors that provide scientifically valuable data rather than merely covering the area.
method: The field is partitioned into grid cells sized by UAV ground coverage. After an initial exploration, each cell receives a scientific utility score based on freshness, redundancy, anomaly likelihood, and model uncertainty. The UAV then optimizes a route to visit high-utility cells under battery and return-to-base constraints.
result: The framework reframes UAV-based data collection as adaptive scientific data management, focusing on the value of information rather than exhaustive sensing.
conclusion: The proposed method aims to improve the efficiency and scientific value of data collection in smart farming, though no experimental results are reported in the abstract.

title: Ulam Rank Aggregation Is Hard To Approximate For Four Rankings
authors: Sk Ruhul Azgor, Diptarka Chakraborty, Le van Cuong, Debarati Das, Mursalin Habib, Tien Long Nguyen
abstract: ArXiv:2609.05874v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the approximability of rank aggregation under the Ulam metric. In the problem, the goal is to find a ranking (permutation) minimizing the sum of its Ulam distances to the input rankings, while in the problem, the objective is to minimize the maximum such distance. We prove that, for every [MATH], it is [MATH]-hard to approximate either Ulam median or Ulam center within a factor of [MATH], even when the input consists of only four rankings. We further show that unless P = NP, neither problem admits a polynomial-time additive approximation scheme. Prior to our work, only the exact versions of both problems were known to be [MATH]-hard, and that too only when the number of input rankings is unbounded [Fischer et al., ESA'25 and Bachmaier et al., J. of Discrete Algorithms'15]. Furthermore, our inapproximability results are optimal in terms of the number of input rankings since for three inputs it is already known to be polynomial-time solvable [Chakraborty, Das, Krauthgamer, SODA'21]. En route, we introduce a new general framework for reducing Boolean constraint satisfaction problems (CSP) to the Ulam median with only four inputs. As a specific instantiation of the reduction framework, we obtain our hardness-of-approximation results. The corresponding hardness for the Ulam center follows from a reduction from the Ulam median.
tldr: This paper proves that approximating Ulam median and Ulam center is NP-hard even for only four input rankings, and that no polynomial-time additive approximation scheme exists unless P=NP.
motivation: Rank aggregation under the Ulam metric is a key combinatorial problem, yet prior hardness results only applied to unbounded numbers of rankings; establishing inapproximability for a constant number is an open question.
method: The authors develop a general framework reducing Boolean constraint satisfaction problems (CSPs) to the Ulam median problem with exactly four inputs, and derive hardness-of-approximation results from a specific instantiation; Ulam center hardness follows via a reduction from Ulam median.
result: For every fixed constant, it is NP-hard to approximate either Ulam median or Ulam center within a constant factor even when the input consists of only four rankings, and neither problem admits a polynomial-time additive approximation scheme unless P=NP.
conclusion: The inapproximability results are optimal in terms of the number of rankings because the problems are polynomial-time solvable for three inputs, showing a sharp complexity threshold.

title: From Review To Authorization: Key-Isolated Threshold Signing For Llm Agents
abstract: ArXiv:2609.05901v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Autonomous LLM agents can turn untrusted content into effectful actions such as payments and permission changes. If the same process interprets this content and controls a reusable signing credential, prompt injection can cross the judgment boundary and reach execution authority. We present KITA, a review-to-authorization architecture that keeps the user's personal secret signing key and every threshold signing-key share outside all LLM processes. Under threshold signature unforgeability and our system assumptions, compromising the proposer and fewer than t reviewer-signer domains cannot produce a valid authorization for a new action without signing contributions from t distinct domains. Thus, any such authorization includes a share from an uncompromised domain, bound to the canonical action and released only after authenticated reviewer approval. This establishes execution-bound authorization integrity. We implement the complete reviewer-to-executor path with a structured-output LLM adapter and threshold BLS. Six system tests validate quorum gating and message binding at this interface, while cryptographic microbenchmarks measure the online signing path and its scaling behavior.
tldr: This paper introduces KITA, an architecture for LLM agents that isolates signing keys and uses threshold BLS signatures to prevent prompt injection from authorizing actions without multi-party approval.
motivation: LLM agents can be hijacked via prompt injection to perform sensitive actions because they control signing credentials, so there is a need to isolate keys and require multiple approvals for execution.
method: The system keeps all signing keys outside LLM processes and requires t distinct reviewer-signer domains to jointly sign each authorization, using threshold BLS and a structured-output LLM adapter.
result: System tests confirm quorum gating and message binding, and microbenchmarks show the signing path scales reasonably, demonstrating practical viability.
conclusion: KITA ensures that any valid authorization must involve an uncompromised domain, thus establishing execution-bound authorization integrity for LLM agents.

title: Evaluating Deep-Search Agents Under Hierarchical Web Evidence Poisoning
authors: Zhongan Bi, Qiwen Wang, Jianrong Jiang, Jigang Ding, Wenwen Xiong, Changhua Meng, Xuanang Gao, Kepeng Lin, Changjiang Jiang, Yiang Chen, Huan Yao, Wei Wang, Zhenyu Ma, Wenhui Dong
abstract: ArXiv:2609.06027v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Search-augmented LLM agents are increasingly used for consumer decisions, making them vulnerable to Generative Engine Optimization (GEO) poisoning. Existing benchmarks largely measure whether manipulated content is retrieved or endorsed, but do not track whether an agent verifies suspicious evidence, revises adopted claims, or recovers before producing its final recommendation. We introduce HAE-GEO, a benchmark that tracks the full trajectory from exposure to recovery under progressively more persuasive Web poisoning. Agents interact via a multi-turn Search-Scrape interface across three attack levels (L1 direct assertion, L2 contextual camouflage, and L3 apparent corroboration), supported by a controlled corpus of 72,039 clean pages and 770 poisoned pages per level spanning 8 product categories and 154 brands. Evaluation combines deterministic behavioral measures with six semantic rubric dimensions. Evaluating 10 agents, we find three recurring patterns: evidence recognition degrades under the corroboration trap; agentic search improves final resistance without improving evidence recognition or utility; and defense prompting increases verification, yet rarely converts verification into recovery.
tldr: This paper introduces HAE-GEO, a benchmark to evaluate deep-search agents' resistance to hierarchical web evidence poisoning across three attack levels.
motivation: Existing benchmarks only measure if manipulated content is retrieved, not whether agents verify, revise, or recover from suspicious evidence.
method: They built a controlled corpus with clean and poisoned pages over multiple attack levels and evaluated 10 agents using deterministic and rubric-based measures.
result: They found evidence recognition degrades under corroboration trap, agentic search improves final resistance but not evidence recognition, and defense prompting increases verification but rarely converts to recovery.
conclusion: The study highlights the need for benchmarks that track the full trajectory from exposure to recovery to assess agent robustness to adversarial web content.

title: It Is Not Yet Another Tool: Creating And Deploying An Agentic Ai Companion In A Security Operations Center
authors: Kritan Banstola, Faayed Al Faisal, Duy Dao, Ryan Irving, Daniel Lende, Xinming Ou
abstract: ArXiv:2609.06250v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Security Operations Centers (SOCs) process large amounts of tickets, most of which are low-interest events not worthy of further investigation. The repetitive nature of this task and similarity of the vast amounts of tickets make it a prime candidate for generative AI-based automation. We created and deployed an agentic AI companion utilizing large language models through fieldwork within a SOC for over one year. The design of the SOC AI companion was driven by researchers' participation and interactions within the SOC's daily work. SOC analysts were invited to use it during the last four months of the fieldwork. We analyzed the analysts' usage of the companion and found that in more than 90% of the cases the companion's outputs were reused by analysts in the ticket's closing report. Our results showed that when designed "in the trenches" with the intended users, a SOC AI companion can go beyond being yet another tool, but rather a system that co-evolves with its human users as it traverses through the various types of workloads. Analysts naturally started to shape the AI companion's behaviors to fit their particular needs. Our data show that the more human analysts shape the AI companion's behaviors, the more they become comfortable trusting the output from the AI system, resulting in improved productivity.
tldr: This paper describes the design and deployment of an agentic AI companion in a Security Operations Center, showing that analysts reused its outputs in over 90% of cases.
motivation: SOCs process many low-interest tickets that are repetitive and time-consuming, making them good candidates for generative AI automation, but existing tools often fail to integrate into daily workflows.
method: The authors conducted fieldwork in a SOC for over a year, iteratively designing an AI companion with analyst participation, and analyzed usage data from the last four months.
result: In over 90% of cases, analysts reused the AI companion's outputs in ticket closing reports, and trust increased as analysts shaped its behavior, leading to improved productivity.
conclusion: An AI companion co-designed with users can go beyond being a simple tool, becoming a system that co-evolves with human users and enhances trust and productivity.

title: Side: Sensor Impersonation Detection At The Edge Via Sequence Prediction
abstract: ArXiv:2609.06271v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Some low-cost Internet of Things (IoT) sensor deployments lack device-level source authentication, leaving them vulnerable to impersonation or injected sensor readings. We present a lightweight approach to sensor impersonation detection in a small proof-of-concept study. We formulate detection as a sequence-prediction problem. A model with three LSTM layers and two fully connected layers is trained only on univariate temperature readings from a genuine sensor, and a window of readings is flagged when its mean absolute prediction error exceeds the mean genuine error by more than six standard deviations. The model is converted to TensorFlow Lite and deployed on an Arduino Nano 33 BLE in three variants, non-quantized (554 KB), 16-bit weight quantized (298.5 KB), and 8-bit weight quantized (185 KB). On a controlled testbed with the impostor sensor placed in a hotter outdoor location, the three variants reached detection accuracies of 99.980%, 99.972%, and 98.206%, and each flagged the change point when a test sequence switched from genuine to impostor data. Quantization made the model smaller but slower in our measurements. The genuine and impostor distributions were well separated, so these results show detection of a controlled distribution shift and should not be read as evidence of general device authentication.
tldr: A lightweight LSTM-based model detects sensor impersonation in IoT by flagging windows with unusually high prediction error.
motivation: Low-cost IoT sensors often lack source authentication, leaving them vulnerable to impersonation or injected readings.
method: An LSTM with three LSTM layers and two dense layers is trained on genuine sensor readings, converted to TensorFlow Lite, and deployed on an Arduino Nano; windows with error exceeding six standard deviations above the mean are flagged.
result: On a controlled testbed, variants (non-quantized, 16-bit quantized, 8-bit quantized) achieved detection accuracies of 99.980%, 99.972%, and 98.206%, respectively, but quantization increased latency.
conclusion: The method detects controlled distribution shifts but is not a general authentication solution.

title: Mars: Detecting Unauthorized Variable Manipulations In Multi-Application Plc Runtimes
abstract: ArXiv:2609.06306v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Programmable Logic Controllers (PLCs) increasingly run multiple applications alongside the main control program, with shared access to PLC variables. Yet, Industrial Control System (ICS) defenses primarily detect malicious updates by checking whether variable values violate expected bounds, without considering which application performed the update. A malicious application can exploit this gap by modifying variables within normal bounds while still driving the physical process toward an unsafe state. Even when such manipulation is detected, operators cannot identify the responsible application because PLCs do not associate variable updates with application identity. We present MARS, an automated framework for application-level authorization and attribution of PLC variable manipulations. MARS profiles applications on an isolated virtual PLC (vPLC) to derive application-specific variable-access policies and uses a shadow vPLC during operation to attribute production-PLC updates to individual applications without instrumenting the production controller. MARS also detects manipulations that occur only on the production PLC and therefore have no corresponding update on the shadow vPLC. We evaluate MARS on manufacturing, chemical, and water-treatment systems against attacks in which unauthorized applications manipulate PLC variables while remaining within normal bounds. Our results show that MARS detects these manipulations and identifies the responsible application.
tldr: MARS is a framework to detect and attribute unauthorized variable manipulations in multi-application PLC runtimes.
motivation: ICS defenses typically ignore which application performs updates, allowing malicious apps to manipulate variables within normal bounds to unsafe states.
method: MARS profiles applications on an isolated virtual PLC to derive access policies and uses a shadow vPLC during operation to attribute production-PLC updates to specific applications.
result: Evaluation on manufacturing, chemical, and water-treatment systems shows MARS detects such manipulations and identifies the responsible application.
conclusion: MARS provides application-level authorization and attribution for PLC variable manipulations, enhancing ICS security.

title: Beyond Qa Matching: Perturbation-Response Fingerprinting Via Probability Distributions For Large Language Models
authors: Jichao Zeng, Yanli Chen, Hanzhou Wu
abstract: ArXiv:2609.06330v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large language models are often instruction-tuned, specialized, quantized, or otherwise transformed, making fine-grained provenance difficult. In this paper, we introduce BReF, a training-free fingerprint that compares how probability distributions over four answer-option labels A/B/C/D move under controlled textual perturbations. For each pair of models, BReF selects 25 jointly responsive probes and compares their perturbation log-ratio (PLR) response directions by global cosine similarity. On a unified benchmark with 34 checkpoints, 22 documented direct-parent relations, and 411 suspect-candidate pairs, BReF retrieves the documented parent in 22/22 cases (MRR=1.0000), with DP-DF AUC 1.0000. Same-family discrimination is harder (DP-SF AUC 0.8969), and paired tests show a significant exact-retrieval gain over a magnitude-only Top-25 control. Together with static, random-probe, permutation, calibration, and transformation-level controls, the results show that strong pooled separation does not guarantee correct parent ranking among closely related checkpoints, verifying the superiority of our work.
tldr: BReF is a training-free fingerprinting method for LLMs that compares probability distribution shifts under perturbations to identify model provenance.
motivation: To determine the provenance of large language models that have been instruction-tuned or quantized, making it difficult to trace their origins.
method: BReF uses 25 jointly responsive probes and compares perturbation log-ratio response directions via cosine similarity to match suspect models to known parents.
result: On a benchmark with 34 checkpoints, BReF retrieved the correct parent in all 22 cases (MRR=1.0) and showed high discrimination, though same-family discrimination was harder.
conclusion: The method demonstrates that response-pattern fingerprints can reliably identify model provenance, outperforming magnitude-only approaches.

title: A Graph Foundation Model For Large-Scale Mimo Detection
authors: Xingyu Zhou, Le Liang, Hao Ye, Jing Zhang, Chao-Kai Wen, Xiao Li, Shi Jin, Wei Zhang
abstract: ArXiv:2609.06361v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large-scale multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) detection is fundamental to modern wireless networks but constrained by performance-complexity trade-offs. Existing detectors, whether classical or learning-based, often fall short in either scalability or generalizability across heterogeneous scenarios. To overcome these limitations, we introduce a wireless-native graph foundation model (GFM) tailored for large-scale MIMO detection. The proposed GFM employs a physics-informed hybrid architecture, integrating the local correlation extraction of message passing neural networks with the global attention of graph Transformers, encoding the physical interference patterns from the expectation propagation algorithm. Via extensive pre-training, this synergy enables the learning of a general-purpose detection mapping scalable across antenna dimensions and channel conditions. For rapid downstream deployment, parameter-efficient fine-tuning is leveraged to adapt the GFM to specific non-ideal system regimes with minimal overhead. To enhance inference efficiency, a mixture-of-experts mechanism is embedded at downstream deployment to dynamically activate only the necessary sub-modules. Evaluations show that the proposed GFM consistently outperforms classical detectors and advanced data-driven baselines in accuracy, configuration generality, and cross-scenario transferability across various challenging zero-shot and few-shot conditions.
tldr: Introduces a wireless-native graph foundation model for large-scale MIMO detection that pre-trains to be generalizable across configurations and supports efficient fine-tuning.
motivation: Existing MIMO detectors, whether classical or learning-based, face performance-complexity trade-offs and lack scalability or generalizability across heterogeneous scenarios.
method: Proposes a graph foundation model combining message passing neural networks and graph Transformers, encoding interference patterns from expectation propagation, with pre-training and parameter-efficient fine-tuning, plus a mixture-of-experts mechanism for inference.
result: Outperforms classical detectors and data-driven baselines in accuracy, configuration generality, and cross-scenario transferability under zero-shot and few-shot conditions.
conclusion: Demonstrates that a graph-based foundation model can provide scalable and adaptable MIMO detection, but the topic is outside the specified research interests.

title: FoldNTT: A Multiplier- And Twiddle-Lean Ntt Core With Formally Verified Arithmetic For Proth Primes
abstract: ArXiv:2609.06412v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Hardware for lattice-based post-quantum cryptography spends a large share of its area on the number-theoretic transform (NTT), dominated by modular multipliers and twiddle storage. FoldNTT is a redesign of the released radix-2 CFNTT accelerator (TCHES 2022) for the Falcon / FN-DSA prime q = 12289 with one hardware multiplier per butterfly instead of three and about half the stored twiddle constants. The Proth shape q = 3*2^12 + 1 turns modular reduction into shift-and-add K-RED folds, and the bit-reversed twiddle table obeys w[N/2+j] = psi*w[j], so half the table is derived without a multiplier. Checking the released RTL against the mathematics also exposed a bug: its inverse transform omits a per-stage halving and returns 2^10*x, which the retrofit corrects. Every arithmetic block is proven by exact-width SMT and compositional SymbiYosys proofs, control-safety invariants by k-induction; the proofs are mutation-tested and the composed transform is validated by simulation, all rerun by CI. On Artix-7 in a fully open flow, the retrofit costs 3->1 DSP48 per butterfly and -50% stored twiddle bits at a whole-core Fmax cost of about 4% (best of three seeds; within the seed-to-seed spread), measured on the released datapath driven by a controller we reconstructed (the reference FSM was never released) and validated by full-core simulation; a sequential core with our own controller builds to a timing-gated Basys-3 bitstream.
tldr: A hardware redesign of an NTT core for the Falcon post-quantum cryptography scheme, reducing multipliers and twiddle storage via formal verification.
motivation: To improve the hardware efficiency of NTT, a critical component in lattice-based post-quantum cryptography, for resource-constrained implementations.
method: The paper proposes FoldNTT, a redesign of a radix-2 CFNTT accelerator, exploiting the Proth prime structure for simplified modular reduction and deriving half the twiddle table without a multiplier, and uses formal verification (SMT, SymbiYosys, k-induction) to ensure correctness.
result: The redesign reduces DSP48 usage from 3 to 1 per butterfly, halves stored twiddle bits, and incurs only a 4% Fmax penalty, with all arithmetic blocks formally verified and validated by simulation.
conclusion: The paper demonstrates a significantly more efficient NTT core for Falcon, backed by formal proof of correctness, which is valuable for practical post-quantum cryptography implementations.

title: Random Algebraic Geometry Codes Approach The Half-Singleton Bound For Insertions And Deletions
abstract: ArXiv:2609.06441v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we study the performance of algebraic geometry (AG) codes against adversarial insertion-deletion (insdel) errors. The half-Singleton bound states that an [MATH] linear code can correct at most [MATH] insdel errors. It was recently proven that random Reed-Solomon codes approach this bound. However, these constructions require the field size [MATH] to grow linearly with the code length [MATH]. We overcome this barrier by extending the probabilistic analysis of general linear insdel codes to AG codes. We demonstrate that curves with many rational points allow for nearly optimal codes over significantly smaller alphabets. We prove the following main asymptotic results: (1) For general smooth complete curves of fixed genus, random AG codes are nearly optimal, that is, they can correct [MATH] insdel errors with high probability over linear-sized fields ([MATH]). (2) By utilizing Hermitian curves, we achieve this optimality over sublinear fields of size [MATH], breaking the linear field size barrier. motivation: Previous constructions for correcting insdel errors required field sizes growing linearly with code length; the goal is to achieve near-optimal error correction with smaller alphabets.
method: The authors extend probabilistic analyses of general linear insdel codes to algebraic geometry codes, utilizing curves with many rational points, including Hermitian curves and García-Stichtenoth towers.
result: They prove that random AG codes can correct n-2k-2 insdel errors with high probability over linear-sized fields, sublinear fields via Hermitian curves, and even constant-size fields independent of n with optimal towers.
conclusion: This work overcomes the linear field size barrier, showing that AG codes achieve nearly optimal insdel error correction more efficiently.

title: Uav Fluid-Antenna Channel Acquisition Under Intra-Scan Channel Aging
authors: Yuanhui Wu, Hao Jiang, Liang Wu, Zaichen Zhang
abstract: ArXiv:2609.06537v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Sequential sounding in UAV fluid-antenna systems (FASs) provides additional spatial information but delays transmission, causing earlier channel observations to age. This paper addresses the resulting information--freshness tradeoff by jointly determining where to probe and when to stop under blockwise hardware constraints. A dynamic Karhunen--Lo\`eve estimator aligns asynchronous measurements with the transmission state, covariance information gain selects feasible probe locations, and an age-discount identity with a local one-more-slot condition characterizes the covariance-level balance between information and freshness. Paired simulations show that temporal alignment recovers most of the lower-tail reliability lost by static stacking, covariance-aware probing ranks highest numerically among the evaluated policies, and optimized one-slot sounding becomes statistically competitive with two-slot alternatives at the highest tested mobility. Within the evaluated schedule family, increasing mobility shifts the competitive operating region toward shorter scans, supporting joint probe-placement and sounding-duration design.
tldr: Presents a method for UAV fluid-antenna channel acquisition that balances information gain and freshness under channel aging.
motivation: Sequential sounding in UAV fluid-antenna systems introduces delay causing earlier observations to age, creating an information-freshness tradeoff.
method: Uses a dynamic Karhunen-Loève estimator to align asynchronous measurements, covariance-based selection for probe locations, and an age-discount condition to balance information and freshness.
result: Simulations show temporal alignment recovers reliability, covariance-aware probing performs best, and optimized one-slot sounding rivals two-slot under high mobility.
conclusion: Supports joint design of probe placement and sounding duration, shifting toward shorter scans at higher mobility.

title: Uniform In Time Propagation Of Chaos For Noisy Mean-field Coupled Maps

Given a Lipschitz one-particle map and interaction term, we prove that, if the lower bound on the noise density is sufficiently large, the [MATH]-dimensional transfer operator [MATH] preserves a dimension-independent class of sub-Gaussian probability measures. title: The Role Of Gradient Modification In Heavy-Tailed Nonconvex Stochastic Min-Max Optimization
authors: Tianxi Zhu, Yi Xu, Xiangyang Ji
abstract: ArXiv:2609.06064v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Stochastic min-max optimization has attracted increasing attention due to its applications in modern machine learning, while existing theoretical studies mainly rely on the bounded variance assumption for stochastic gradients. Under heavy-tailed noise, where stochastic gradients only possess a finite [MATH]-th moment for [MATH], gradient clipping or normalization is commonly believed to be necessary to guarantee convergence. In this work, we revisit stochastic min-max optimization under heavy-tailed noise and provide a comprehensive theoretical study of stochastic gradient descent ascent (SGDA). We first show that vanilla SGDA, without any modification to its update rule, can converge under heavy-tailed noise in both nonconvex-strongly-concave (NC-SC) and nonconvex-concave (NC-C) settings, establishing the first convergence guarantees for SGDA in these regimes. Beyond unregularized problems, we further investigate regularized stochastic min-max optimization, where directly incorporating gradient normalization into proximal updates is nontrivial due to the incompatibility between normalization and proximal structures. We overcome this difficulty by developing new clipping-free algorithms, i.e., Stoc-TRGDAM and Stoc-TRGDmax, and they both can achieve the optimal dependence on the target accuracy without using gradient clipping.
tldr: This paper analyzes stochastic min-max optimization under heavy-tailed noise, showing that vanilla SGDA can converge without gradient clipping and proposes clipping-free algorithms for regularized settings.
motivation: To address the assumption that gradient clipping is necessary for convergence in heavy-tailed stochastic optimization, and to handle regularized min-max problems where clipping is incompatible with proximal updates.
method: Provides convergence analysis of vanilla SGDA in nonconvex-strongly-concave and nonconvex-concave settings, and develops two new clipping-free algorithms (Stoc-TRGDAM and Stoc-TRGDmax) for regularized problems.
result: Establishes the first convergence guarantees for SGDA under heavy-tailed noise and achieves optimal dependence on target accuracy without using gradient clipping.
conclusion: Gradient modification like clipping is not always required for convergence in heavy-tailed min-max optimization, contrary to common belief.

title: Large Language Models As Strategic Bidding Agents In P2p Energy Trading Markets
authors: Ismail Lotfi, Ali Ghrayeb, Haitham Abu-Rub
abstract: ArXiv:2609.05462v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Peer-to-peer (P2P) energy trading markets rely on double auction mechanisms to match prosumers and consumers in smart grid distribution networks. However, the strategic behavior of bidding agents in such markets remains not fully explored, particularly in repeated settings with bounded rationality. This paper proposes a novel framework that integrates large language models (LLMs) as reasoning-driven bidding agents in repeated P2P energy double auctions. We compare the performance of three bidding strategies: random bidding, an [MATH]-greedy multi-armed bandit (MAB) approach, and an LLM-based strategy. Simulation results show that the LLM-based strategy achieves superior cleared trading volume over the first episodes compared to [MATH]-greedy MAB and random bidding baselines, eliminating the exploration burn-in period that statistical learning algorithms inherently require before converging to productive price arms. Importantly, when tested in an environment different from the one used during learning, the performance of the [MATH]-greedy strategy drops significantly, while that of the LLM-based bidding strategy continue to achieve higher surplus and successful trades. Nevertheless, the LLM's advanced contextual reasoning also gives rise to an important market dynamic. In a homogeneous population of LLM agents, sellers increasingly exploit buyers' rational outside options to drive clearing prices above the Nash equilibrium, resulting in a progressively more asymmetric allocation of surplus in favor of sellers that does not converge within the observed time horizon.
tldr: This paper proposes using LLMs as strategic bidding agents in P2P energy double auctions, showing they outperform greedy bandit and random strategies in trading volume but cause asymmetric surplus allocation favoring sellers.
motivation: To address the lack of exploration of strategic bidding behaviors in repeated P2P energy markets with bounded rationality, and to leverage LLMs' reasoning capabilities for adaptive bidding.
method: The authors simulate three bidding strategies (random, ε-greedy multi-armed bandit, and LLM-based) in a repeated double auction framework, comparing their performance across trading volume, surplus, and adaptability.
result: The LLM strategy eliminates exploration burn-in, achieving higher cleared trading volume and better performance in new environments, but in homogeneous LLM populations it drives prices above Nash equilibrium, causing sellers to exploit buyers' outside options and creating persistent surplus asymmetry.
conclusion: LLM agents can improve bidding efficiency but may destabilize market fairness, suggesting a need for regulatory mechanisms or mixed populations to mitigate power imbalances.

title: A Complex Structure On $S^2\times S^4$
authors: Shengtao Guo, Ethan X. Fang, Junwei Lu
abstract: ArXiv:2609.05504v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We show that [MATH] admits a complex structure. motivation: To determine which manifolds admit complex structures; specifically, it was an open question whether S^2 × S^4 admits one.
method: Starting with a modular family of complex two-tori related to a triangle group, they consider a monodromy-invariant index-two superlattice and compactify the family. result: They show that the constructed compact complex threefold is diffeomorphic to S^2 × S^4, thus establishing that S^2 × S^4 admits a complex structure.
conclusion: The existence of a complex structure on S^2 × S^4 is established, resolving a known question.

title: On Besov And Triebel-Lizorkin Spaces Associated With The Grushin Operator
authors: Sayan Bagchi, Nishta Garg, Rahul Garg
abstract: ArXiv:2609.05940v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this article, we define classical and non-classical Besov and Triebel--Lizorkin spaces associated with the Grushin operator with or without drift. We establish various characterisations of these spaces, and study their complex interpolation, embedding properties, and fractional Leibniz rules.
tldr: This paper defines and studies Besov and Triebel-Lizorkin spaces associated with the Grushin operator, establishing characterizations, interpolation, embeddings, and fractional Leibniz rules.
motivation: To extend the theory of function spaces to degenerate elliptic operators like the Grushin operator, which is of interest in harmonic analysis and PDEs.
method: The authors define the spaces using the Grushin operator and its semigroup, then prove characterizations, complex interpolation, embedding properties, and fractional Leibniz rules.
result: They successfully define classical and non-classical Besov and Triebel-Lizorkin spaces for the Grushin operator and establish several key analytical properties.
conclusion: The paper contributes to the theory of function spaces in subelliptic settings, but it is not related to any of the specified research directions.

title: Robustness Evaluation And Detection Of Transferable Adversarial Attacks In ML-Based Nids
abstract: ArXiv:2609.06012v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Machine learning-based network intrusion detection systems (ML-based NIDS) are vulnerable to adversarial evasion, where malicious samples are perturbed to evade detection and be misclassified as benign. Despite growing research on adversarial attacks and defenses for ML-based NIDS, comparative evaluations of multiple attack types, detection models, and defense strategies under a common setting remain limited. In this paper, we evaluate eight adversarial evasion attacks, fifteen detection models, and three representative defense strategies using the NF-UQ-NIDS dataset, which includes recent traditional and IoT network traffic with twenty distinct attack categories. The evaluation compares model performance on clean test data and on robustness evaluation sets that include adversarial samples, analyzes attack success consistency across models, and examines the effect of defense strategies on adversarial robustness. To support model comparison, we introduce the Robustness Index (RI), a compact comparative metric that rewards high balanced accuracy and macro-F1 score computed on the robustness evaluation set while penalizing high attack success rate (ASR). We further present AR-NIDS, a two-stage framework that uses an adversarially trained ensemble to distinguish normal, attack, and adversarial samples, followed by an adversarial attack classifier to identify the attack type. Under the evaluated transfer-based setting, the proposed adversarially trained ensemble achieves the strongest overall trade-off between classification performance on the robustness evaluation set and evasion resistance, reducing the average ASR from 0.41 to 0.03 and achieving an RI of 0.98.
tldr: This paper evaluates adversarial evasion attacks on ML-based network intrusion detection systems and proposes an adversarially trained ensemble framework to improve robustness.
motivation: ML-based NIDS are vulnerable to adversarial evasion, but comparative evaluations of multiple attacks, models, and defenses under a common setting are lacking.
method: The paper conducts a comprehensive evaluation using the NF-UQ-NIDS dataset, comparing eight attacks, fifteen detection models, and three defenses, and introduces a Robustness Index (RI) and an AR-NIDS framework with an adversarially trained ensemble followed by an attack classifier.
result: The adversarially trained ensemble reduces average attack success rate from 0.41 to 0.03 and achieves an RI of 0.98, outperforming other defenses.
conclusion: The proposed framework provides a strong trade-off between classification performance and evasion resistance in transfer-based adversarial settings.

title: Reliable iToF Depth Sensing Via Sensor-Intrinsic Uncertainty Modeling And State-Space Restoration
authors: Yansong Du, Yutong Deng, Yuting Zhou, Zhancong Xu, Yingjia Lu, Mengdi Wang, Feiyu Jiao, Bangyao Wang, Zhaoxiang Jiang, Xun Guan
abstract: ArXiv:2609.05507v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Indirect time-of-flight (iToF) cameras provide compact and cost-effective dense depth measurements, but their ranging accuracy is often degraded by sensor-intrinsic uncertainty under practical imaging conditions. Spatially uniform or range-only Gaussian perturbations cannot accurately reproduce the range-dependent and signal-dependent noise characteristics of real iToF measurements, leading to a synthetic-to-real gap for learning-based restoration. To address this problem, we propose a joint depth-uncertainty modeling and restoration framework for reliable iToF sensing. A sensor-intrinsic depth-uncertainty model is first developed from calibrated tap responses, returned-signal levels, and sensor noise statistics through a depth-oriented weighted least-squares formulation. The resulting pixel-wise uncertainty is used for heteroscedastic depth synthesis and uncertainty-aware restoration supervision. Based on this heteroscedastic data synthesis, we further develop a U-shaped restoration network with Depth Visual State Space (DVSS) blocks, which combine long-range state-space modeling with convolutional spatial-channel refinement for structure-preserving depth recovery. Experiments on synthetic data and measurements captured by an in-house iToF prototype validate the proposed uncertainty model under varying range and returned-signal conditions. Controlled comparisons with fixed and range-aware Gaussian noise, together with evaluations on U-Net, Restormer, and DVSS, further demonstrate that the proposed synthesis consistently benefits different restoration backbones. The complete framework achieves 40.85~dB PSNR and 2.54 mm MAE on the synthetic test set, and 35.42 dB PSNR and 4.87 mm MAE on real iToF measurements.
tldr: This paper presents a framework for reliable indirect time-of-flight depth sensing by modeling sensor-intrinsic uncertainty and using a state-space restoration network.
motivation: Existing noise models for iToF cameras fail to capture actual range-dependent noise, causing a synthetic-to-real gap in learning-based restoration.
method: They construct a pixel-wise uncertainty model from sensor statistics and use it for data synthesis and supervision, then apply a U-shaped network with DVSS blocks that combine state-space and convolutional processing.
result: The method achieves better PSNR and MAE on both synthetic and real iToF data compared to baselines.
conclusion: The uncertainty-aware modeling and restoration improve the accuracy of iToF depth measurement under practical conditions.

title: One Equation Allocates Playing Time In Competitive Team Sports: The Rulebook Sets The Arithmetic And The League Sets The Habit
abstract: ArXiv:2609.05584v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Every team sport that lets a team replace players rations the replacements, and the ration settles who plays and for how long. Across eight codes, three in both sexes, we measure how playing time is allocated and find one equation behind it, complete in the one-way codes, its terms separating what the rulebook fixes from what a competition chooses. Under scarcity every league behaves alike: loaded starters are kept on at the same rate on four continents. Under freedom each expresses a preference, and the size of a league's departure is priced near one-for-one by what its own withdrawal minute prices (lambda = 0.87, 95% interval 0.54 to 1.21, twelve leagues), a law confirmed in four out-of-sample predictions and refused in one. The ordering of leagues by appetite persists across a rule change, and club wealth does not price it. Rules are the geometry of a competition; culture is its material.
tldr: This paper analyzes playing time allocation in team sports and finds a single equation that describes it based on rulebook constraints and league preferences.
motivation: To understand how playing time is distributed in competitive sports and whether there is a universal pattern.
method: They measure playing time allocation across eight sports codes in both sexes, analyzing the effects of substitution rules and league behavior, and fit an equation with parameters separating fixed rules from league choices.
result: They find a single equation that holds across leagues, with league-specific preferences captured by a parameter lambda (with a confidence interval), and they validate it with out-of-sample predictions.
conclusion: Playing time allocation is determined by an arithmetic set by rulebooks and a habit set by leagues; rules create the geometry, and culture (league preference) provides the material.

title: WolfSociety: Understanding Collective Risk From Harmful-Agent Scaling In Financial Agent Societies
authors: Lejun Zhang, Sarah Lu-Liang, Xin Jiang, Muning Wen, Weinan Zhang, Shangding Gu
abstract: ArXiv:2609.05591v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Safety evaluations typically focus on individual agents, but interacting agents can spread harmful information and influence the environment in which later decisions are made. We study how collective failure changes with harmful-agent fraction and society size in a controlled financial agent society, where agents communicate over a social network and trade in a shared market. In the primary financial scenario, collective failure requires broad harmful diffusion together with severe price dislocation or liquidity stress. Across all tested society sizes, failure remains rare at low harmful fractions but rises sharply over a narrow range. As society size grows from N=100 to N=2000, the harmful fraction associated with a 50% failure probability decreases from 4.7% to 2.2%, while the corresponding number of harmful agents increases from approximately 5 to 44. In contrast, when the number of harmful agents is held fixed, their impact becomes weaker as the society grows. Controlled interventions further show that broader network reach shifts the collapse boundary toward lower harmful fractions, whereas stronger conformity alone has little effect. To characterize these effects, we introduce Agent Society Dynamics, a finite-size framework for relating harmful-agent fraction, society size, and interaction structure to collective failure. Overall, our results reveal a nonlinear, size-dependent collapse transition in financial agent societies, showing that collective failure depends not only on the prevalence of harmful agents but also on the size and interaction structure of the surrounding society. Code is available at [URL].
tldr: This paper studies collective failure in financial agent societies as a function of harmful-agent fraction and society size, introducing a framework called Agent Society Dynamics.
motivation: Safety evaluations typically focus on individual agents, but interacting agents can spread harmful information and influence collective behavior. The authors aim to understand how collective failure emerges in a controlled financial setting.
method: They simulate a financial agent society where agents communicate over a social network and trade in a shared market, varying harmful-agent fraction, society size, and network structure. They introduce a finite-size framework (Agent Society Dynamics) to relate these factors to collective failure.
result: Collective failure is rare at low harmful fractions but rises sharply over a narrow range; as society size grows, the harmful fraction needed for 50% failure probability decreases (from 4.7% at N=100 to 2.2% at N=2000). Broader network reach lowers the collapse boundary, while stronger conformity has little effect.
conclusion: Collective failure in financial agent societies is nonlinear and size-dependent, depending not only on the prevalence of harmful agents but also on society size and interaction structure.

title: The Collective Dynamics Of Online Harassment
authors: Brian C. Keegan Benjamin Freixas Emery
abstract: ArXiv:2609.05754v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Fringe online message boards are often studied in the context of the extreme ideology that they produce. So far, however, not much of this research has focused on direct real-world harm in the all-too-common form of collective harassment. We directly analyze the complex dynamics of KiwiFarms, an online message board dedicated largely to the harassment of individuals from vulnerable communities. We conduct exploratory analyses of the hyperlink structure of the platform and linguistic changes over time, and prospective modeling of thread size. After establishing this broader picture of the complex traits of the system, we observe the temporal evolution of community-specific vocabulary, finding that the community's framing of their harassment targets persistently evokes more danger in the early 2020s than the late 2010s. We lastly find that early thread-growth behavior is predictive of longer-term thread virality. We discuss the implications for broader understanding of toxic online behavior and threat assessment, and make the case for studying fringe platforms as complex systems with significant societal impact.
tldr: This paper analyzes the collective dynamics of online harassment on KiwiFarms, examining hyperlink structure, linguistic changes, and predictors of thread virality.
motivation: To understand direct real-world harm caused by fringe online platforms, specifically collective harassment of vulnerable communities.
method: Exploratory analyses of hyperlink structure and linguistic changes over time, plus prospective modeling of thread size and temporal evolution of community-specific vocabulary.
result: Found that the community's framing of harassment targets evoked more danger in the early 2020s than the late 2010s, and early thread growth behavior predicts long-term thread virality.
conclusion: The study demonstrates the value of treating fringe platforms as complex systems with significant societal impact, with implications for threat assessment and understanding toxic online behavior.

title: Price Dislocations, News Citations, And Epistemic Leverage On Polymarket
abstract: ArXiv:2609.06005v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Prediction-market probabilities increasingly appear in news coverage, yet little is known about which market movements become news or how much trading money sits behind the numbers journalists quote. Unlike a poll, a market price can be moved by anyone willing to trade, so the cost of manufacturing a number that circulates as news bears directly on the information environment. We link 173.7 million signed Polymarket trades to news coverage from 2024-2025. From 6,990 articles mentioning prediction-market venues, an LLM-based, human-validated matcher extracts 1,582 sentences quoting market odds and attributes 918 to the specific market whose price they cite. We then detect 44,976 price dislocations, movements of at least five percentage points backed by concentrated one-sided trading, and ask whether a market is cited more often afterward. In the days after a dislocation, a market's citation rate is about 33% higher than its matched baseline (log citation-rate ratio [MATH], permutation [MATH]), robust to binary and Poisson count outcomes. Yet move size is not the strongest predictor of citation: prominence dominates (standardized [MATH] vs. [MATH] for move size). Finally, we combine the dollar flow behind a given price change with observed citation rates into a metric we call epistemic leverage, the dollars needed to move a market five points and have the move cited. It stays near \$0.7-1.0 million across prominence quintiles, because cheaper-to-move markets are proportionally less likely to be cited. The implied threat model centers not on the long tail of cheaply moved markets but on the few prominent markets newsrooms treat as informational infrastructure, where a seven-figure price of influence sits within the budgets of actors with a large stake in the quoted number. We release aggregate event-study data and validation materials.
tldr: This paper studies how price dislocations in prediction markets (Polymarket) lead to news citations and quantifies the 'epistemic leverage' - the dollars needed to move a market price and have it cited.
motivation: To understand how market manipulation can influence news reporting, since prediction-market probabilities are increasingly cited in news.
method: They link 173.7 million Polymarket trades to news articles, detect price dislocations (movements ≥5 points with concentrated one-sided trading), and measure citation rates after dislocations. They also compute epistemic leverage by combining dollar flow and citation rates.
result: After a dislocation, citation rates increase by ~33%, but prominence matters more than move size. Epistemic leverage stays around $0.7-1.0 million across prominence quintiles.
conclusion: The threat of manipulation is not in cheap markets but in prominent markets where a seven-figure investment can influence widely-cited numbers.

title: Optimal Practice Allocation Under Learning Saturation
abstract: ArXiv:2609.05501v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A saying attributed to Bruce Lee unfavorably contrasts a martial artist who has practiced ten thousand kicks once each with another who has practiced a single kick ten thousand times. We read the saying as implicitly raising a question about how to allocate a fixed practice budget among several skills, and we show that the answer is governed by two ingredients: the shape of the learning curve that converts practice into skill, and the rule by which separate skills are aggregated into overall effectiveness. Neither ingredient alone settles the matter. Our central result reduces the multivariable allocation problem to the maximization of a single scalar \(\eff(x)=f(x)^{p}/x\); under a simple uniqueness and divisibility condition, every optimal practice schedule is , dividing the budget equally among a definite number of skills. The optimal number of skills is then determined by a transparent criterion equating the elasticity of the learning curve to the reciprocal of the aggregation parameter. Hard-saturation models, heterogeneous learning rates, a sharp specialization threshold, and a genuinely intermediate optimal repertoire all follow as consequences.
tldr: This paper develops a framework for optimally allocating a fixed practice budget among multiple skills based on learning curve shapes and aggregation rules.
motivation: The Bruce Lee quote motivates the question of how to split practice time across skills to maximize overall effectiveness.
method: Formalizes the multivariable allocation problem and reduces it to maximizing a scalar function, deriving conditions for optimal schedules.
result: Under uniqueness and divisibility conditions, equal allocation among a definite number of skills is optimal, with the number set by a criterion involving the learning curve elasticity.
conclusion: Provides insights into practice allocation, including specialization thresholds and intermediate optimal repertoires.

title: Analysis Of Pairs In A Generalized Deck Of Playing Cards
abstract: ArXiv:2609.05538v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this study, we analyze the number of pairs (i.e., two cards of the same rank) in a set of cards randomly selected from a deck of playing cards. While the standard deck of playing cards comprises 52 cards excluding the joker with 4 suits and 13 ranks, our analysis considers a generalized deck where the numbers of suits and ranks can be set arbitrarily. We derive the exact formulas for the mean and variance of the number of pairs in a given number of cards randomly selected from this generalized deck, expressed using the Gauss hypergeometric function. Moreover, we derive the asymptotic behavior of the mean and variance as the number of ranks tends to infinity.
tldr: This paper derives exact formulas for the mean and variance of the number of pairs in a randomly drawn set of cards from a generalized deck, expressed via Gauss hypergeometric functions, and analyzes asymptotics.
motivation: To generalize the analysis of pairs in a standard deck to arbitrary numbers of suits and ranks, providing a combinatorial/probabilistic framework.
method: Derivation of exact formulas for mean and variance using combinatorial arguments and Gauss hypergeometric functions, along with asymptotic analysis as the number of ranks tends to infinity.
result: Exact expressions for mean and variance in terms of hypergeometric functions, and asymptotic behaviour derived.
conclusion: Provides a complete characterization of pair counts in generalized decks.

title: A Simple Method Of Computing Riemann-type Integrals
abstract: ArXiv:2609.05562v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The "Riemann-type integrals" of the title are not a single new integral, but the family of classical constructions -- Riemann, Riemann-Stieltjes, Young-Kondurar, complex-analytic, and It\^o -- unified by one elementary method. We give a simple argument computing the Riemann integral of a polynomial directly, establishing the fundamental theorem of calculus for polynomials and then continuous functions. The same idea extends to the real line, the complex plane, the multidimensional case, the Riemann-Stieltjes integral, and the It\^o integral of a polynomial of a Wiener process (more generally, a continuous semimartingale), recovering the classical It\^o formula. The contribution is methodological: a single algebraic telescoping identity, paired with an estimate on a quadratic remainder term, drives every case. What changes is only the remainder's fate: it vanishes identically for polynomials on [MATH]; it vanishes in the limit under a quadratic-variation condition [MATH] on [MATH] and for H\"older paths; and for a continuous semimartingale it survives as the quadratic variation producing the It\^o correction -- except for a planar Brownian motion, or more generally a conformal martingale, where an algebraic cancellation inside the complex square removes it again. We regard this last point -- that the It\^o correction and its cancellation in the conformal case are two instances of the same quadratic remainder, not unrelated facts -- as the paper's most distinctive observation. The manuscript has three parts: Part I develops the core method on [MATH] and [MATH]; Part II extends it deterministically to the multidimensional, Riemann-Stieltjes, and H\"older (Young-Kondurar) cases; Part III extends it to the stochastic setting.

motivation: To provide a simple and unified approach to compute classical integrals such as Riemann, Riemann-Stieltjes, and Itô integrals, highlighting a common structure.
method: The method uses a telescoping identity and a quadratic remainder term that vanishes in different limits depending on the smoothness of the integrand, leading to the integral formulas.
result: The method recovers classical results including the fundamental theorem of calculus, Itô's formula, and also shows that the Itô correction and its cancellation in conformal martingales arise from the same remainder.
conclusion: The paper offers a novel pedagogical and methodological perspective, but it has no direct relation to quantum information sciences.

Still, as a positive result, we prove that every bounded linear operator on a separable complex Banach space for which a non-fixing invariant probability measure exists, has to have some approximate point spectrum on the unit circle minus [MATH].

motivation: The question of whether invariant probability measures imply the existence of eigenvalues has been open since Flytzanis (1995) and later asked by Grivaux et al. The author aims to answer this question.
method: The method involves constructing or analyzing bounded linear maps on complex separable Hilbert spaces to produce counterexamples and proving a general theorem for Banach spaces using spectral theory.

conclusion: The results settle the open question and provide a positive spectral consequence for invariant measures in more general spaces.

title: Flatness Of The Generic Under-Actuated 6-Degrees-of-Freedom Unmanned Surface Vessel
authors: Peter J. Vassiliou Taylor J. Klotz
abstract: ArXiv:2609.05785v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The flatness of the under-actuated unmanned surface vessel with circular hull-shape (``the hovercraft") has long been known. We resolve the long-standing open problem: whether the generic under-actuated 6-degrees-of-freedom (dof) unmanned surface vessel (gUSV) admits a feedback linearization. Lie symmetries of the gUSV are used to construct a dynamic feedback linearization, explicit flat outputs and flat parametrization, for all hydrodynamic parameter values. In this generic case the dynamic compensator has order 6, in contrast to the hovercraft vessel whose dynamic compensator has order 4.
tldr: This paper proves that generic under-actuated 6-degree-of-freedom unmanned surface vessels admit feedback linearization by constructing explicit flat outputs using Lie symmetries.
motivation: The flatness of hovercraft-type vessels is known, but the generic USV case was an open problem; resolving it is crucial for advanced control design in marine robotics.
method: The authors utilize Lie symmetries of the generic USV (gUSV) to derive a dynamic feedback linearization, including explicit flat outputs and parametrization.
result: They show that the gUSV admits a dynamic feedback linearization with a compensator order of 6, whereas the hovercraft has order 4.
conclusion: The long-standing question is answered affirmatively: the generic 6-DOF USV is flat, enabling potentially simpler control strategies.

title: Race, Exchange, Improve: Finding High-quality Mip Solutions Quickly
abstract: ArXiv:2609.05954v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Mixed-integer programming (MIP) is a cornerstone in applied optimization, both in industry and academia. Recently, there has been increased attention to finding strong primal solutions quickly. This is reflected, for example, in the development of the NVIDIA cuOpt solver and, most recently, in the new MIPFEAS benchmark, which has a tight time limit of 600 seconds and evaluates solvers based on how quickly they find high-quality primal solutions. This article introduces a MIP portfolio parallelization scheme, focusing on efficiently exchanging information between its workers. We present two implementations of this scheme: one built directly into the open-source MIP solver SCIP, and an external one, which we call ReXi. ReXi is currently the fastest non-commercial solver in the MIPFEAS benchmark, followed by the SCIP-integrated implementation. Moreover, we present new versions of both implementations that considerably outperform their predecessors on the MIPFEAS benchmark.
tldr: This paper proposes a MIP portfolio parallelization scheme to quickly find high-quality primal solutions, implemented in SCIP and an external solver named ReXi.
motivation: The paper addresses the increasing demand for fast discovery of strong primal solutions in mixed-integer programming, as highlighted by new benchmarks with tight time limits.
method: They develop a parallelization scheme focusing on efficient exchange of information between workers, realized both within the SCIP solver and as an external implementation called ReXi.
result: ReXi is currently the fastest non-commercial solver on the MIPFEAS benchmark, and the new versions of both implementations considerably outperform their predecessors.
conclusion: The proposed portfolio parallelization effectively accelerates high-quality primal solution finding, establishing ReXi as a top-tier non-commercial solver.

title: Looking For Bidding Teammates: A Game-Theoretic Model Of Stranger Collusion In Peer Review
abstract: ArXiv:2609.05444v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Paper bidding is the entry point to reviewer assignment at large CS conferences: reviewers declare interest, combined by an optimizer with automated affinity scores. Reviewers who have never met recruit each other online, exchange identifiers, bid on each other's papers, and reciprocate with inflated scores. Existing collusion models assume already-trusted colleagues; open recruitment removes that assumption and the mechanism that made such arrangements work. We give the first game-theoretic model of collusion in peer review, the : a four-stage game covering recruitment, exchange of identifiers under risk of being reported, unverifiable bidding, and reciprocal reviewing. The model predicts the arrangement cannot form: once assigned a partner's paper, writing the inflated review is pure cost, since the benefit depends on the partner's own decision. Reciprocation is never individually rational, for any payoffs, and the arrangement unwinds. What closes the gap is enforcement, not incentives: authors see their own reviews, deadlines recur every few months, and the group remembers who reciprocated. We derive the condition under which inflation is sustainable, the detection rate above which no partnership survives, and show effort enters both. On a calibrated end-to-end conference simulation, no detector we test exceeds [MATH] against an attacker who camouflages bids, spreads them around a ring, and manipulates affinity; a two-person arrangement is worth [MATH] points of acceptance probability; and the harm is distributional, not aggregate: [MATH] honest papers are displaced while mean quality moves by only [MATH], so no summary statistic reveals it. Randomized assignment is the one defense reaching enforcement itself, making a partner who never bid indistinguishable from one who bid and lost.

motivation: Existing collusion models assume pre-existing trust among colleagues, but open recruitment of strangers is more realistic and requires a new model.
method: Develops a four-stage game covering recruitment, identifier exchange, unverifiable bidding, and reciprocal reviewing, and derives conditions for sustainable inflation and detection thresholds.

conclusion: The paper suggests that randomized assignment is the only defense that reaches enforcement, as it makes bidding irrelevant, and provides a new framework for understanding collusion risks in peer review.
